jobs.title: Sr. Project Manager - Supply Chain (Remote with Heavy Travel)
jobs.description:
The Senior Project Manager - Supply Chain is responsible for delivering large-scale implementation projects for Harbor Freight’s Supply Chain.  This role leads cross-functional teams – including resources from Distribution, Engineering/Facilities, Inventory, Transportation, IT, Real Estate, Finance, and others – through the entire life cycle of a project from intake through completion.  Potential key projects expected for this role include new distribution facilities, supply chain system implementations, large-scale material handling projects, and high-impact process improvement initiatives involving interdisciplinary teams.

Reporting to the Sr. Director, Supply Chain Project Management Office, the Sr. Project Manager - Supply Chain will be responsible for planning and executing multiple, concurrent Supply Chain projects and/or initiatives. The role owns project outcomes and ensures projects are delivered on time, within outlined scope, and within approved budget.  He or she will also be responsible for coordinating project deliverables, aligning stakeholders, and communicating with all impacted partners. The Sr. Project Manager must be a strong leader, detail-oriented, and an excellent communicator with both project teams & leadership.  It is essential that the candidate can adapt to challenges, stay within capital budgets, meet timelines, and deliver high levels of quality/service.  Building strong relationships with key internal business partners is also critical to the role’s success.

Duties and Responsibilities

Responsible for all aspects of project management through the entire lifecycle, including, but not limited to: developing business cases, chartering, scoping, requirements gathering, project plan and schedule creation, status reporting, issue resolution, project resource allocation, document approval tracking and management, risk and dependencies, project costs, and financial analysis.
Accountable for successful project transition to operations, benefits validation, lessons learned documentation and applying lessons learned to future projects.
Has ownership for compliance with project governance, meeting key performance indicators (schedule, scope, budget), and contribution to Supply Chain Objectives & Key Results (OKR).
Creates and maintains strong relationships with internal partners, external partners, key stakeholders and cross-functional leaders.
Actively coaches, mentors and develops project managers and team members.
Collaboratively leads cross-functional project teams and business partners to develop and execute project deliverables.
Effectively directs the work of the project team & business partners on a week-to-week basis.
Creates cohesive project plans and schedules with identifiable critical path, task dependencies, and major milestones.
Works with key cross-functional partners to develop and execute a comprehensive transition plan to hand-off project ownership from the project team to long term business owners.
Sets deadlines, defines roles & responsibilities (RACI), assigns owners, monitors progress, and drives accountability.
Prepares and delivers project status reports and executive updates.
Adept at establishing efficient and disciplined processes, methodologies, & governance.  Works with colleagues to continually improve those processes.

Scope

Staff supervision and development:  Indirect only
Decision making:  Participate in planning business objectives, provide consultation & expert advice, provide data, facilitates decision with appropriate business owners and leadership
Travel: Expect to travel between 20-40% of weeks in a year
Flex Designation:  Anywhere

The anticipated salary range for this position is $126,700 – $190,100 depending on location, knowledge, skills, education and experience. This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus. In addition, we offer comprehensive and competitive benefits to Associates (and their families) such as medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term and long-term disability. Eligible Associates are able to enroll in our company’s 401k plan. Associates will accrue paid time off up to 236 hours per year (inclusive of PTO, floating holidays, and paid holidays). Paid sick time up to 80 hours per year unless otherwise required by law.

jobs.description:
Acute Care Technology

At ZOLL, we're passionate about improving patient outcomes and helping save lives.

We provide innovative technologies that make a meaningful difference in people's lives. Our medical devices, software and related services are used worldwide to diagnose and treat patients suffering from serious cardiopulmonary and respiratory conditions.

ZOLL Data Systems, a division of ZOLL Medical Corporation, is a healthcare software solutions provider that empowers hospital, EMS and Fire, and billing/accounts receivable (AR) teams to deliver more—from better patient outcomes to operational efficiencies and greater revenue capture. Our business exists to help save more lives through data-driven innovation and interoperability, opening new pathways for our customers to achieve the highest levels of care, collaboration, and reimbursement.

ZOLL Medical does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need ZOLL immigration sponsorship (e.g. H1B, TN, STEM, OPT, etc.) either now or in the future.

Job Summary

The Project Manager supports the successful customer-facing implementation of ZOLL’s technology solutions in fast-paced emergency healthcare environments. In this role, you will plan, coordinate, and manage implementation activities in partnership with experienced project managers, cross-functional teams, and EMS customers who operate under constant pressure. Success requires strong organizational skills, a willingness to learn, and comfort working in environments where processes, timelines, and project details may continue to evolve. This role is ideal for a developing project manager who is eager to build foundational project management skills, gain exposure to the product development lifecycle, and grow within a mission-driven organization supporting emergency medical services.

Essential Functions

Provide management oversight for each project assigned
Ability to manage multiple projects or project phases simultaneously
Manage customer relationship during the project
Understand and communicate the project schedule to internal and customer project teams and resources
Manage to the contract to assure compliance
Proactively identify and mitigate risk
Maintain the project plan and its associated components with frequent updates to internal and customer stakeholders
Support projects where not all requirements are fully defined at the outset, partnering with internal teams and customers to help clarify needs as implementations progress.
Apply a learning mindset to new or unfamiliar situations, seeking guidance and incorporating feedback to navigate changing priorities and implementation challenges.
Assure successful acceptance and closure of the project
Maintain a high standard of customer service, evidenced by consistently achieving high customer satisfaction ratings upon project completion
Assure accurate revenue recognition and accounting relating to each project assigned, as appropriate
Understanding of and adherence to internal accounting and security requirements, HIPAA and revenue recognition standards
Travel to customer sites (local, national, and international) to attend and conduct project kick-off, status, planning, technical requirement gathering, and project closure meetings as necessary.
Represent the company in a professional and competent manner, always, as corporate liaison
Manage customer expectations and develop internal and external relationships
Continue to learn and apply project management methodologies and best practices.
Willingly engage in self and professional improvement training utilizing both internal and external training tools and classes.
Ongoing contribution to team knowledge sharing

Required/Preferred Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in business, IT, healthcare, or related field preferred
3+ years of external customer-facing project related experience required
Experience in IT, healthcare, or software support is highly desirable.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Base understanding of PMI concepts
Proficiency using personal computers and applications such as Salesforce, Office 365, Excel, SharePoint and other software
Detail orientated and strong organizational skills
Maturity of judgment under pressure and the ability to work independently and make sound decisions
Strong desire to learn project management practices, healthcare workflows, and technical concepts, with the ability to apply new knowledge quickly.
Ability to negotiate successfully with customers and vendors
Balance structure with flexibility to support successful outcomes in real-world implementation scenarios.
Strong written and verbal communications skills with excellent professional presence
Solid business acumen with a high level of decision-making skills and the ability to maintain a proactive approach to continuous process improvement
Ability to manage numerous activities within time constraints and deadlines

The Annual Salary For This Position Is

$74,000.00 to $110,000.00

Factors which may affect starting salary include geography, skills, education, experience, and other qualifications of the successful candidate. Details of ZOLL's comprehensive benefits plans can be found at www.zollbenefits.com.

Company Description

Improving healthcare through innovative technology is at the core of Intelerad’s work. Our scalable medical imaging platform connects clinicians to a powerful imaging ecosystem that is fast, smart, and tapped into the data they need, no matter their location. We’re focused on delivering a best-in-class medical image management solution that improves provider efficiency, decreases the cost of healthcare, and improves the overall health of populations.

Intelerad offers one of healthcare’s most comprehensive imaging and analytics platforms. Headquartered in Raleigh, NC and Montreal, Intelerad has nearly 700 employees located in offices across six countries. The company empowers nearly 2,000 healthcare organizations around the world with the speed, scalability, and simplicity needed to increase business performance while, most importantly, improving patient outcomes. Intelerad’s modern enterprise solutions have been acknowledged by a Best in KLAS recognition, ranking #1 for PACS Asia/Oceania in the 2021 Best in KLAS: Global Software (Non-US) report. To learn more, visit intelerad.com and follow Intelerad on LinkedIn and Twitter.

Job Description

Role Overview

The Program Manager III is a principal-level delivery leader responsible for the governance, execution, and strategic oversight of large-scale, complex programs within Intelerad's Professional Services organization. Operating at the enterprise tier, this role partners directly with C-suite client stakeholders to drive successful implementation of Radiology and Cardiology Healthcare IT solutions, establishing program management frameworks and leading cross-functional teams to ensure consistent delivery excellence. The Program Manager III serves as a trusted advisor to both internal leadership and external clients, accountable for program financial performance, risk management, and the continuous elevation of delivery practices across the portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Drive enterprise program governance and delivery excellence by designing and implementing program management frameworks, overseeing interconnected project portfolios, and ensuring all initiatives are executed in alignment with client operational goals and Intelerad's delivery standards.
Lead executive-level client relationships by serving as the primary strategic advisor to C-suite and senior client stakeholders, managing complex expectations, directing steering committee sessions, and resolving critical escalations with diplomacy and measurable outcomes.
Own program financial performance and risk by managing budgets of $5M+, establishing risk mitigation frameworks in partnership with cross-functional teams, and ensuring program financials remain aligned with contracted scope and business objectives.
Develop and elevate the program management practice by defining and implementing methodologies and best practices, mentoring Project Managers and Program Managers across all levels, and leading enterprise-wide transformation and standardization initiatives.
Contribute to strategic business development by proactively identifying growth opportunities within existing client relationships, participating in strategic planning activities, and supporting the expansion of Intelerad's Professional Services footprint.

Qualifications

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent experience
10+ years of progressive experience in Program or Project Management roles
5+ years of experience leading enterprise-scale programs in Healthcare IT or comparably complex environments
Demonstrated experience managing program budgets of $5M or greater
PMP or Program Management Professional (PgMP) certification, or equivalent demonstrated competency

Preferred Qualifications & Special Requirements

Master's degree (MBA, MHA, or equivalent), or equivalent experience
Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification
Experience with enterprise Healthcare IT software implementations, including Radiology and/or Cardiology solutions
Proficiency with Agile, Waterfall, and hybrid delivery methodologies
Change management expertise and organizational development experience

Travel Requirements: This position requires up to 30% travel throughout North America, with occasional international travel

This job description is not a comprehensive list of tasks or requirements and Intelerad reserves the right to change it at any time.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

for our Office of Chief Technology Officer (OCTO)
to join the AI Centre for Enablement (C4E) team.

Why This Role Matters:

The AI Control Plane (AICP) is Pearson's flagship investment in AI infrastructure: a multi-year programme that closes Pearson's AI governance gap, accelerates how teams ship AI value, and builds the strategic know-how to keep AI cost-effective as usage scales. It delivers enterprise-wide visibility into Pearson's AI estate—what is deployed, what it costs, where it creates value, and what we should do next. AICP sits inside OCTO's AI Centre for Enablement (C4E).
This is a deliberately blended role. Roughly 70% is technical programme management of a major cross-organisation investment, working across Pearson business units and corporate functions including engineering, security, and legal. Roughly 30% is product leadership for an internal 'data product'—the enterprise AI telemetry dashboard that turns Pearson's AI investment decisions from opinion-led to evidence-led. You will drive how that dashboard looks and how it gets built, working with a cross-functional engineering pod inside OCTO.
You run the day-to-day delivery of AICP—from architecture handoff through business-unit onboarding to global scale—and act as product owner for the enterprise AI telemetry dashboard. You free the engineering and architecture leads from coordination overhead so they can focus on what only they can do.
As a member of OCTO AI C4E and Pearson, you are expected to embody and role model our leadership dimensions:

Live Our Purpose:
You align your values, actions, and goals with Pearson's mission. You connect daily work to our broader purpose and make decisions that reflect a deep understanding of our strategy.

Simplify the Complexity:
You navigate ambiguity and distil complexity into clear, actionable plans. You help teams focus and execute in a dynamic environment.

Carry Our Culture:
You foster customer centricity, high performance, and strong collaboration. You lead with integrity and contribute to inclusive, high-performing teams.

Deliver Results:
You set ambitious goals and execute with quality, precision, and speed. You hold yourself accountable for outcomes and measurable impact for learners and stakeholders.

What You'll Do

Translate AICP strategy into executable plans—workstreams, owners, milestones, dependencies—across Pearson business units and corporate functions including engineering, security, and legal.
Run programme cadence and reporting: status, risks, decision logs, steering committees, working groups. Coordinate external delivery partners against contractual commitments and commercial terms.
Drive business-unit adoption of the governance and security capabilities AICP delivers—discovery, risk tiering, monitoring—against ambitious year-end onboarding targets.
Act as product owner for the enterprise AI telemetry dashboard: define personas and the questions they need answered, prioritise the backlog, and ship v1 covering an initial set of enterprise tools. Build prototypes and design mocks where it helps the engineering team move faster.

Who You Are:

Customer-centric: you keep business-unit outcomes and leadership decisions—not vendor outputs—as the success measure.
Hands-on and AI-fluent: you mock up a dashboard, prototype with modern AI tools, and drive design decisions yourself rather than waiting for engineers to read your mind.
Pragmatic and persistent: you create clarity where none exists and close follow-up loops before they become escalations.

What You Bring

5+ years of programme or project management in technology, with cross-functional reach across product, engineering, and operations.
Product management or product-owner experience for technical or data products—someone who has shipped a v1 of something internal, not just managed a backlog.
Vendor coordination experience with major enterprise technology partners (e.g. hyperscalers, large system integrators).
Working understanding of AI, data engineering, or cloud architecture at a level sufficient to translate technical constraints into delivery plans and product decisions.

What You'll Gain:

Lead-PM/PdM role on a Board-visible AI infrastructure programme sponsored by OCTO leadership.
Ownership of the enterprise AI telemetry product—Pearson's first enterprise view of "what AI is doing for us".
Direct collaboration with engineering, security, and business-unit leaders across Pearson, and visibility across OCTO and the Chief Data & AI Office.

Why Pearson?

At Pearson, we don't just build careers—we accelerate them. This position provides visibility across the Office of the Chief Technology Officer and the AI C4E, with a clear path into broader technical and strategic roles.

Groundwater & Environmental Services, Inc. (GES)
, an industry leader with a reputation for excellence in providing environmental consulting, engineering, compliance, and technical field services to clients in diverse market sectors, seeks an experienced and motivated Environmental Project Manager
to join our growing team in Richmond, Virginia. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who thrives in a leadership role and enjoys working on complex projects with diverse technical and regulatory demands across Virginia and the surrounding region.

What You’ll Do

As an Environmental Project Manager at GES, you’ll take full ownership of a dynamic portfolio of projects, with a strong focus on environmental investigation, remediation, and regulatory compliance in Virginia. You’ll lead technical teams, serve as a primary client contact, and ensure projects are delivered on time, on budget, and to the highest quality standards.

Manage a diverse portfolio of environmental investigation and remediation projects (primarily in Virginia).
Supervise and mentor technical staff; assign resources and oversee the preparation of reports, proposals, and project deliverables.

Lead project planning, execution, and budgeting; track performance against financial goals.
Review and author technical documents, including complex site characterizations and remedial action plans.

Collaborate with internal teams and business development staff to support consistent, high-quality service and foster new opportunities.

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Geology, Environmental Science, or a related field.
5–10+ years of relevant experience, including investigation, remediation, reporting, and client/project management.
Strong working knowledge of Virginia environmental regulations and accompanying guidance documents.
Proven experience authoring and reviewing complex technical documents and reports.
Demonstrated success in managing clients, project budgets, and personnel.
Skilled in strategic thinking, problem-solving, and maintaining long-term client relationships.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills; strong attention to detail.

jobs.description:
Senior Project Manager – Rail

Location:
UK or Republic of Ireland | Location flexible

Join Us in Shaping the Future of Rail Infrastructure

Are you an experienced project manager with a strong background in rail or complex transport infrastructure? Join Tetra Tech and take ownership of high-profile projects that support the future of rail across the UK and Republic of Ireland.

You will work with clients, technical specialists, delivery partners and stakeholders to lead projects from early development through design, consents, delivery and handover. This is an opportunity to apply your technical leadership, commercial judgement and project management expertise to complex, multidisciplinary rail programmes.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

As Senior Project Manager, you will lead complex rail projects or substantial project workstreams through the full project lifecycle, establishing and managing the project scope, delivery strategy, baseline programme, resources, budget and reporting arrangements. You will coordinate multidisciplinary teams across rail systems, civil and structural engineering, stations and depots, environmental services, and stakeholder and third-party interfaces. The role involves managing project risks, opportunities, issues, decisions, change and commercial performance, as well as coordinating design reviews, assurance, approvals, procurement and construction interfaces to ensure deliverables are properly integrated, coordinated and accepted at each stage. You will also promote safe design and delivery in line with applicable UK or Irish duties, project assurance requirements and site arrangements.

Your Impact in This Position

Your leadership will help ensure that complex rail projects are delivered safely, efficiently and to the required quality, programme and commercial outcomes. You will provide clear direction to multidisciplinary project teams, build effective relationships with clients, operators, infrastructure managers, contractors and statutory bodies, and resolve technical, organisational and delivery interfaces before they affect project outcomes. You will maintain strong control of programme, cost, risk, change and resources, lead client meetings, provide accurate and concise progress reporting, escalate decisions at an early stage, and maintain clear records of commitments, actions and change. You will also support the development of bids and fee proposals, while mentoring project managers and assistant project managers and contributing to the growth of project delivery capability across the business.

Core Capabilities

Project Leadership and Delivery

Lead complex rail or transport infrastructure projects from early development through design, consents, delivery and handover, ensuring that scope, programme, resources and budgets remain under control.

Multidisciplinary Coordination

Direct and coordinate technical teams across rail systems, civil and structural engineering, stations, depots, environment and stakeholder interfaces.

Risk, Change and Commercial Management

Manage risk, opportunity, issue and decision registers, while overseeing change, forecasting outturns and applying sound commercial judgement to protect project outcomes.

Stakeholder and Client Leadership

Communicate technical and project information clearly to senior stakeholders. Lead client meetings, manage relationships and resolve interfaces with operators, infrastructure managers, contractors and statutory bodies.

Safety, Assurance and Team Development

Promote safe design and delivery, coordinate assurance and approvals, support bids and fee proposals, and mentor project managers and assistant project managers.

Essential

Qualifications & Experience

Substantial experience managing rail or similarly complex transport infrastructure projects.
Experience working across multidisciplinary design and delivery interfaces.
Demonstrable experience managing programme, cost, risk, change and client relationships.
Sound commercial judgement and experience forecasting project outcomes.
Proven ability to lead project teams and communicate technical matters clearly to senior stakeholders.
A relevant degree or equivalent experience in engineering, construction, project management or a related discipline.

Desired

Professional project management or engineering accreditation, such as APM, PMI, Engineers Ireland or membership of a relevant chartered institution.
Experience working with Network Rail, Transport for London, Iarnród Éireann, Transport Infrastructure Ireland or other rail authorities.
Experience working with NEC contracts.
Experience managing statutory approval processes.
Experience of supporting bids, fee proposals and the development of less experienced project managers.

Working Environment

This role can be based in the UK or Republic of Ireland, with location flexibility depending on the project and vacancy requirements.

The role will involve travel to project sites and client locations across the UK and Ireland as required. You will be expected to apply the relevant local duties, standards and client assurance arrangements for each project.

The specific office base and working pattern, including expectations regarding office attendance and any hybrid, remote or flexible working arrangements, will be confirmed for the individual vacancy.

Why join Tetra Tech?

Tetra Tech is a leading provider of consulting and engineering services working across the full project lifecycle worldwide. We have a wide range of expertise across our teams, providing a global support network with a personalised approach to client relationships to better understand where we can add value. We provide a collaborative environment that supports individual performance, innovation, and creativity.

W e support public and private sector clients on local, national, and international projects to deliver sustainable and resilient solutions. Our operations in the UK, Ireland, and the Netherlands include more than 6,000 employees who are Leading with Science® to solve our clients’ most complex problems.

In alignment with the Equality Act 2010, we will make reasonable adjustments to support candidates and employees requiring additional arrangements. This could include adaptations to work schedules, training approaches, or the physical workspace. Please inform us if you need any accommodations during the recruitment process or in your day-to-day role.

Recruitment Agencies

We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners to assist us when required and do not acknowledge any speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on this list and any submitted will be taken as a gift. Please refer to the careers page on our website if you require any further information.

Sopra Steria
offers tailored, end-to-end corporate technology and software solutions to help clients make bold choices and deliver results. Successfully so! With more than 56.000 colleagues in 30 countries, we rank as Europe’s leading digital solutions provider. Some of the most successful companies in Europe rely on our technology due to our commitment to innovation, collaboration, and value in business development.

The world is how we shape it. Let’s shape it together.

Job Description

The Senior IT Programme Manager
will serve as the single accountable executive for a flagship European Commission programme in the domains of Dataspace and Artificial Intelligence. Operating at the intersection of cutting-edge technology policy and large-scale public-sector delivery, this individual will bear ultimate responsibility for scope, schedule, budget, quality, risk, and stakeholder satisfaction across a multi-partner consortium delivering transformative digital infrastructure for Europe.

This is a highly visible, strategically critical position requiring a rare combination of deep EU institutional knowledge, technical credibility in Dataspace and AI, and the executive presence to lead complex negotiations at the highest levels of the European Commission and across 27 Member State administrations.

Key Responsibilities:

Programme Leadership & Governance
Establish and chair the Programme Governance Board, ensuring alignment with European Commission priorities and contractual obligations.
Define and own the integrated programme master plan (IMP), managing interdependencies across all workstreams and consortium partners.
Drive end-to-end programme execution from inception through deployment and operational handover, maintaining a €100M+ budget baseline.
Apply and adapt EU programme management frameworks (e.g., PM²) and Agile-at-scale methodologies as appropriate.
Own programme-level risk register, issue log, and escalation procedures; proactively identify and mitigate threats to delivery.
Consortium Leadership & Partner Management
Lead the operational governance of a consortium comprising four partner organisations, including sub-contractor oversight and contractual compliance.
Chair and facilitate Consortium Management Committees, Technical Steering Committees, and Joint Programme Boards.
Manage partner performance, monitor KPIs, and enforce SLAs and contractual obligations under the prime contract.
Resolve cross-partner conflicts, resource contention, and scope boundary disputes with authority and diplomacy.
Foster a collaborative, high-performance consortium culture aligned with shared programme objectives.
EU Institutional Stakeholder Management
Serve as the primary relationship owner and executive point of contact for European Commission DG counterparts.
Build and sustain trusted advisory relationships with Commission programme sponsors, IT Steering Committees, and EC senior management.
Engage proactively with EU country stakeholders across 27 Member States, coordinating national rollout activities and managing country-level expectations.
Represent the programme in high-level review meetings, governance forums, and political-level briefings.
Navigate the EU institutional landscape with sensitivity to political dynamics, procurement regulations, and EU financial regulations.
Dataspace & AI Programme Delivery
Oversee technical delivery of Dataspace architecture components.
Drive AI programme workstreams in alignment with the EU AI Act, the AI Office, and Commission AI strategies.
Ensure technical solutions are interoperable, standards-compliant (EUCS, ETSI, W3C, ISO), and aligned with EU security requirements.
Collaborate with Enterprise Architects, Data Engineers, Developers, testers and AI specialists to validate technical direction and manage delivery risk.
Financial Management
Own and manage the full programme budget (€100M+), including baseline, forecast, earned value management (EVM), and variance reporting.
Oversee procurement activities under EU Financial Regulations and applicable framework contracts.
Prepare and defend financial reports, Monthly Progress Reports (MPR), and Quarterly Management Reviews for the Commission.
Ensure auditability of programme expenditure in accordance with EC Internal Audit Service (IAS) standards.
Quality, Compliance & Reporting
Implement and maintain the Quality Management Plan (QMP) in accordance with ISO 9001 and EC quality standards.
Ensure compliance with GDPR, NIS2, EU AI Act, and relevant Commission security policies (ITSM, ISMS).
Produce executive-level programme dashboards, milestone reports, and presentations for senior EC stakeholders.
Manage lessons learned, continuous improvement, and knowledge transfer processes throughout the programme lifecycle.

Qualifications

Minimum 15 years of IT programme/project management experience, with at least 8 years in senior/lead programme management/director roles.
Demonstrated track record of successfully delivering EU Commission IT programmes at scale (€50M+ budget), ideally with DGs like DIGIT, TAXUD, CONNECT, or equivalent.
Proven experience managing and leading multi-partner consortia as prime contractor in EU public procurement contexts.
Deep operational knowledge of EU procurement frameworks, framework contracts, and EU Financial Regulations.
Hands-on experience with EU programme management methodology PM² or equivalent, including governance, reporting, and documentation standards.
Experience engaging with EU Member State government stakeholders and national administrations across multiple countries.
Substantial technical exposure to Dataspace architectures and/or AI programme delivery in a public sector or regulated environment.

Highly Desirable

Direct experience on EU Dataspace programmes (e.g., GAIA-X, IDSA-aligned, European Health Data Space, Mobility Data Space, or similar).
Knowledge of EU AI initiatives including the EU AI Act implementation, the European AI Office, and AI regulatory compliance frameworks.
Familiarity with EC digital infrastructure programmes such as CEF Digital, the Digital Europe Programme (DEP), or Horizon Europe ICT projects.
Experience with EC interoperability frameworks (EIF) and the ISA²/Interoperable Europe Act.
Understanding of cloud sovereign requirements under EUCS and European cloud initiatives.

Education & Certifications

Master's degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Public Administration, or a related field.
Programme/Project Management: PgMP (PMI), MSP (AXELOS), or PM² Advanced certification required.
Desirable: PMP, PRINCE2 Practitioner, ITIL 4 Foundation, Scrum@Scale, or SAFe certification.
EU institutional training or EPSO-related qualifications are an advantage.

Work at the intersection of business strategy and technology transformation.
Contribute to large-scale, high-impact digital programmes.
Be part of a leading European consulting and digital services organisation.

What we offer?

A strategically pivotal role shaping Europe's digital infrastructure for a decade to come.
Direct engagement at the highest levels of the European Commission and EU Member State governments.
Leadership of one of the most complex and high-profile EU IT programmes currently in execution.
Competitive executive compensation package benchmarked to the Brussels senior IT programme management market.in a leading European IT integrator.

Pearson, the world's leading learning company, is hiring a Program Manager, AI Control Plane
for our Office of Chief Technology Officer (OCTO)
to join the AI Centre for Enablement (C4E) team.

Why This Role Matters:

The AI Control Plane (AICP) is Pearson's flagship investment in AI infrastructure: a multi-year programme that closes Pearson's AI governance gap, accelerates how teams ship AI value, and builds the strategic know-how to keep AI cost-effective as usage scales. It delivers enterprise-wide visibility into Pearson's AI estate—what is deployed, what it costs, where it creates value, and what we should do next. This is a deliberately blended role. Roughly 70% is technical programme management of a major cross-organisation investment, working across Pearson business units and corporate functions including engineering, security, and legal. Roughly 30% is product leadership for an internal 'data product'—the enterprise AI telemetry dashboard that turns Pearson's AI investment decisions from opinion-led to evidence-led. You will drive how that dashboard looks and how it gets built, working with a cross-functional engineering pod inside OCTO.
You run the day-to-day delivery of AICP—from architecture handoff through business-unit onboarding to global scale—and act as product owner for the enterprise AI telemetry dashboard. You free the engineering and architecture leads from coordination overhead so they can focus on what only they can do.
As a member of OCTO AI C4E and Pearson, you are expected to embody and role model our leadership dimensions:

Live Our Purpose:
You align your values, actions, and goals with Pearson's mission. You connect daily work to our broader purpose and make decisions that reflect a deep understanding of our strategy.

Simplify the Complexity:
You navigate ambiguity and distil complexity into clear, actionable plans. You help teams focus and execute in a dynamic environment.

Carry Our Culture:
You foster customer centricity, high performance, and strong collaboration. You lead with integrity and contribute to inclusive, high-performing teams.

Deliver Results:
You set ambitious goals and execute with quality, precision, and speed. You hold yourself accountable for outcomes and measurable impact for learners and stakeholders.

What You'll Do

Translate AICP strategy into executable plans—workstreams, owners, milestones, dependencies—across Pearson business units and corporate functions including engineering, security, and legal.
Run programme cadence and reporting: status, risks, decision logs, steering committees, working groups. Coordinate external delivery partners against contractual commitments and commercial terms.
Drive business-unit adoption of the governance and security capabilities AICP delivers—discovery, risk tiering, monitoring—against ambitious year-end onboarding targets.
Act as product owner for the enterprise AI telemetry dashboard: define personas and the questions they need answered, prioritise the backlog, and ship v1 covering an initial set of enterprise tools. Build prototypes and design mocks where it helps the engineering team move faster.

Who You Are:

Customer-centric: you keep business-unit outcomes and leadership decisions—not vendor outputs—as the success measure.
Hands-on and AI-fluent: you mock up a dashboard, prototype with modern AI tools, and drive design decisions yourself rather than waiting for engineers to read your mind.
Pragmatic and persistent: you create clarity where none exists and close follow-up loops before they become escalations.

What You Bring

5+ years of programme or project management in technology, with cross-functional reach across product, engineering, and operations.
Product management or product-owner experience for technical or data products—someone who has shipped a v1 of something internal, not just managed a backlog.
Vendor coordination experience with major enterprise technology partners (e.g. hyperscalers, large system integrators).
Working understanding of AI, data engineering, or cloud architecture at a level sufficient to translate technical constraints into delivery plans and product decisions.

What You'll Gain:

Lead-PM/PdM role on a Board-visible AI infrastructure programme sponsored by OCTO leadership.
Ownership of the enterprise AI telemetry product—Pearson's first enterprise view of "what AI is doing for us".
Direct collaboration with engineering, security, and business-unit leaders across Pearson, and visibility across OCTO and the Chief Data & AI Office.

Why Pearson?

At Pearson, we don't just build careers—we accelerate them. This position provides visibility across the Office of the Chief Technology Officer and the AI C4E, with a clear path into broader technical and strategic roles.

jobs.description:

Bolt is shaping a future where cities are built for people, not cars. What started as an ambitious project of a 19-year-old in 2013 has grown into a global mobility platform used by more than 200 million customers and 4.5 million driver and courier partners across 50 countries.

From ride-hailing and food delivery to scooters, e-bikes, and car-sharing, Bolt helps people move through cities every day. Small, autonomous teams drive this work, combining the speed and ownership of a startup with the scale of a global technology company backed by more than €1bn in funding.

And we're just getting started.

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗷𝗼𝗶𝗻 𝗕𝗼𝗹𝘁?

Build the future of mobility and help transform how people live and move in cities.
Tackle challenges at scale that span technology, operations, regulation, and growth.
Take real ownership early. Small, lean teams mean your decisions matter from day one, and you'll learn fast alongside some of the best people in the industry.
Join one of Europe's leading technology companies, backed by world-class investors including Sequoia.

𝗔𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗼𝗹𝗲

Our Central Safety Team monitors and prevents risks that could cause real-world harm to users.

As Program Manager, Safety Processes & Enforcement, you'll own the translation layer between safety policy and operational execution: converting policy intent into enforcement standards, account restriction decisions and case-handling processes that Customer Support agents can apply consistently across every case and every market, supported by automation where appropriate.

You'll own the suspension matrix that determines the enforcement logic for each type of violation, the SOP library that tells support agents how to get there, and the specification work that makes those processes ready for automation, with human oversight built in.

𝗠𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗮𝘀𝗸𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗲𝘀:

Own the suspension matrix and severity classification: define and maintain the enforcement ladder that maps each violation type and severity level to an account action for both riders and partner drivers, with one shared definition of severity used for enforcement decisions and incident response.
Build and maintain the SOP library for all safety issue areas, making sure every policy position has a process agents can follow and no process contradicts the enforcement standards. Write processes ready for automation (clear decision trees, defined inputs and outputs, explicit exception and fallback paths) and work with Product and Legal to specify rules-engine logic and automation-assisted enforcement flows, with human review built in.
Own the quality rubric and calibration standards for safety case handling, and own appeals standards by defining how appeals are assessed and what can overturn an enforcement decision.
Drive enforcement consistency: run regular audits, measure where outcomes differ across agents and markets, and lead the fixes.
Work with Safety Policy to make sure standards reflect policy intent, and with Local Safety Operations on local process deviations, making sure each one is documented, justified and checked against the global standard. Report on enforcement consistency, process coverage and automation readiness against team KPIs.

𝗔𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝘆𝗼𝘂:

Proven experience in Trust & Safety, risk management, policy operations or a comparable field, including direct ownership of enforcement policy or operational process design at scale.
Demonstrated experience building or overhauling an SOP library, enforcement framework or suspension matrix used by a large operational team, and writing process specifications for automation or working alongside Product and Engineering on rules engines.
Working knowledge of regulation affecting account enforcement and automated decision-making, such as GDPR, the EU Platform Work Directive and the Digital Services Act.
Deep knowledge of enforcement policy design and policy-to-process translation, with end-to-end ownership of the enforcement framework: you anticipate where standards will drift or break under volume and fix it before it becomes an incident, using case data, appeals data and quality metrics to see where standards are failing in practice.
Strong collaboration and influencing skills across product, legal and operations teams, building agreement without formal authority and holding the line on enforcement consistency under commercial or operational pressure, while managing interdependent workstreams in the right order (standards before processes, processes before automation) and adapting to evolving priorities.

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝘆𝗼𝘂'𝗹𝗹 𝗹𝗼𝘃𝗲 𝗶𝘁 𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲

At Bolt, using AI daily is a baseline expectation for everyone. If there's a faster, smarter way to do your work, we expect you to find it. You're still responsible for the output, so the standard stays high when using AI tools.

Experience is great, but what we really look for is drive, intelligence, and integrity. So even if you don't tick every box, please consider applying!

!

About the role and what you'll be doing: 

As a Principal Project Manager (Consultant) in Delivery Management, you will lead complex programs and strategic client engagements across the full software development lifecycle, helping clients realize sustainable business value from technology investment and transformation.  
You will combine program delivery leadership with strong consulting capability, acting as a trusted adviser to senior and C-level client stakeholders. You will be a proactive, commercially aware and influential leader who creates clarity in ambiguity, anticipates systemic challenges and mobilizes teams and stakeholders around successful outcomes.

Curiosity and openness to innovation: actively seeking out and experimenting with new platforms, tools, and AI-driven approaches to improve delivery efficiency, team collaboration, and client outcomes.

10+ years of experience leading enterprise technology delivery programs, software development initiatives, or digital transformation engagements.  
Demonstrated experience delivering cloud transformation, application modernization, microservices, and enterprise platform initiatives.  
Strong understanding of SDLC practices, DevOps, CI/CD pipelines, release management, and operational readiness.  
Expertise in Agile as well as more traditional delivery frameworks, and a good understanding of when to leverage practices from each to benefit project delivery.

Proven ability to manage project and program budgets, financial forecasting, profitability, and commercial performance.  
Experience managing Fixed Price, Time & Materials, and Managed Services engagements.  
Strong risk management, dependency management, and governance expertise.  
Exceptional communication, facilitation, negotiation, and executive presentation skills.  
Proven ability to influence stakeholders at all organizational levels, including senior executives.  
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with a focus on business outcomes.  
Experience leading geographically distributed and cross-functional teams.  
Demonstrated success creating collaborative team environments and driving accountability for results.  
Ability to identify opportunities for continuous improvement and implement scalable delivery practices.  
Commitment to mentorship, team development, and delivery excellence.  

Preferred Qualifications

Experience delivering solutions on Microsoft Azure and other public cloud platforms.  
Experience within consulting, or professional services environments  
Experience supporting pre-sales activities, statement-of-work development, and solution estimation.

Experience managing global delivery programs across multiple regions and time zones.  

Why Ensono? Ensono is a place to make better happen – for our clients and for your career. jobs.title: Project Manager, People Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A)
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Total Rewards Strategy & Enablement (TR S&E) team translates people strategy into business impact, building the infrastructure, programs, and systems that make Total Rewards work at scale. We bridge strategy and execution, partnering with People leadership and cross-functional teams across Finance, Legal, and the business to turn ambiguous problems into durable programs.

What you’ll do

We’re looking for a collaborative, action-oriented Project Manager to join the Total Rewards Strategy and Enablement team. In this role, you’ll lead business-critical People projects, with a primary focus on mergers and acquisitions (M&A).

Bringing an acquired business into Stripe requires coordinated work across Total Rewards, People Partners, Recruiting, People Operations, Legal, Finance, and Corporate Development. You’ll project manage the People workstream from diligence and integration planning through close and post-close execution. You’ll turn deal-specific decisions into clear plans, ownership, milestones, and risk-management approaches.

You’ll coordinate functional owners across People workstreams, establish plans and dependencies, and step into the work when needed to unblock progress or close critical gaps. Your work will support transaction timelines, reduce business disruption, and create a consistent experience for acquired Stripes.

You’ll build People M&A’s capabilities through repeatable playbooks, infrastructure, and cross-training. This individual contributor role is well suited to someone who can bring structure to ambiguity and move between strategy and execution.

Responsibilities

Project manage People M&A workstreams from diligence and planning through close and post-close execution. Workstreams may include organizational alignment, employee data, onboarding, recruiting, and people program integration.
Serve as a central coordination point across Total Rewards, People Partners, People Operations, People Systems, Recruiting, People Support, Corporate Development, Legal, Finance, and Corporate Technology.
Align plans, dependencies, decisions, and accountability with transaction timelines.
Develop and run integration and change-management plans that give functional leads, acquired Stripes, and other affected audiences the information and support they need at each stage of a transaction.
Identify cross-functional dependencies, risks, and blockers early. Coordinate resolution and escalate issues when needed to protect integration timelines and the Stripe experience.
Establish feedback and support mechanisms for acquired Stripes, including surveys, office hours, and centralized support channels. Use feedback to improve integration plans and change-management approaches.
Build and improve People M&A’s infrastructure, including project plans, templates, checklists, playbooks, reporting, and retrospective documentation.
Build capability across People workstreams through documentation, cross-training, and shared practices that support more consistent future integrations.
Support other business-critical and transformational projects across Total Rewards and the People team as needed.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

You have 7+ years of project or program management experience at a global company, including 2+ years project managing workstreams within the M&A lifecycle, including diligence, integration planning, close readiness, and post-close integration.
You have experience leading complex, cross-functional programs from planning through execution and building repeatable program infrastructure, such as integration playbooks, project-plan templates, readiness checklists, risk logs, or retrospective processes.
You have a track record of turning ambiguous problems into structured, repeatable programs. You’re comfortable building new programs in a scaling environment while improving and standardizing how work gets done.
You have excellent written and verbal communication skills. You can write a one-page executive update, a decision memo tailored to stakeholders, and a step-by-step operator playbook with equal fluency. You guide project teams through complex work in a direct, approachable, and inclusive way.
You can manage senior cross-functional stakeholders across Total Rewards, People Partners, People Systems, Recruiting, Corporate Development, Legal, and Finance. You know when to build alignment, raise a risk, and escalate.
You’re comfortable working with data and systems such as Workday and Greenhouse. You use data to clarify decisions, communicate recommendations, and define requirements with People Systems partners.
You focus on the experience of acquired Stripes and the teams operating the program, not only on program artifacts.
You can manage competing priorities and adapt in a fast-paced environment. You work effectively independently and across teams, bring structure to complexity, and follow through on the details that make a program successful.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with change management frameworks, such as the Prosci ADKAR Model, and applying them to employee or operational change.
Project or program management certification or training, such as Project Management Professional (PMP), Lean, Six Sigma, or a comparable methodology

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $127,600 - $191,400. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

Please find our California applicant personal information notice here.

The application window will remain open for 100 days after the Job Post is published. However, this opportunity will remain open based on the needs of the business, which may cause the application window to close before or after the 100-day mark.

Bank Secrecy Act: Remains cognizant of and adheres to Wings policies and procedures, and regulations pertaining to the Bank Secrecy Act.

jobs.description:
About Us

Clayco is a full-service, turnkey real estate development, master planning, architecture, engineering, and construction firm that safely delivers clients across North America the highest quality solutions on time, on budget, and above and beyond expectations. With $8.1 billion in revenue for 2025, Clayco specializes in the "art and science of building," providing fast track, efficient solutions for mission critical, industrial, life sciences, power & energy, aviation, commercial, institutional, residential and sports & entertainment related building projects.

The Role We Want You For

We are seeking a talented and motivated Business Intelligence Analyst to join our dynamic Data Analytics team. As a Business Intelligence Analyst at Clayco, you will play a crucial role in analyzing complex data sets, developing impactful data visualizations, and delivering valuable insights to support strategic decision-making. This position requires a unique combination of BI development skills and data analysis expertise.

The Specifics of the Role

Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define data requirements and develop innovative solutions that align with business objectives.
Utilize data visualization best practices to create compelling and intuitive visual representations of data, tailored to various stakeholders and business questions.
Apply strong analytical skills to extract meaningful insights from large datasets, using both quantitative and qualitative analysis techniques.
Partner with business stakeholders to understand their needs, define data context, and provide detailed data-driven recommendations.
Develop a deep understanding of our back-end data architecture, including JD Edwards and related data structures, leveraging curated data assets and querying databases to explore and find relevant data for analysis.
Ensure data accuracy and reliability by conducting thorough data validation and contextualization.
Contribute to the design and ongoing development of our BI platforms, ensuring optimal performance, security, and usability.
Effectively communicate insights and recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences using professional verbal and written communication skills.
Translate business requirements into detailed technical requirements, creating clear documentation and test plans for technical testing and User Acceptance Testing (UAT).
Provide support and backup for analytics engineering and data science functions as needed.

Requirements

Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (Computer Science, Information Systems, Statistics, etc.) or relevant experience
5+ years of professional experience as a Business Intelligence Developer, Data Analyst, or related role.
Proficiency in data visualization tools such as Tableau (preferred), with experience in PowerBI/Qlik/DOMO considered acceptable.
Strong command of SQL, including ability to query ERP schemas directly (experience with JDE F-tables a strong plus); knowledge of Python and/or R is a plus.
Demonstrated ability to translate complex data into clear and actionable insights.
Excellent analytical skills with a keen attention to detail.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with technical and business teams.
Proven track record of delivering high-quality results in a fast-paced and deadline-driven environment.
Self-motivated, proactive, and eager to learn and grow within the field of business intelligence and data analytics.
Experience with JD Edwards (JDE) preferred; familiarity with JDE business views
Experience designing or consuming semantic/business views to expose ERP data for BI consumption preferred; understanding of governed data layer concepts is a plus.

Some Things You Should Know

This position will service our clients in St. Louis, MO.
No other builder can offer the collaborative design-build approach that Clayco does.
We work on creative, complex, award-winning, high-profile jobs.
The pace is fast!

2025 Best Places to Work – St. Louis Business Journal, Los Angeles Business Journal, and Phoenix Business Journal.
2025 ENR Top 400 – Top Data Center Contractor (Top 3).
2025 ENR Top 100 Design-Build Firms – Design-Build Contractor (Top 5).
2025 ENR Top 100 Green Contractors – Green Contractor (Top 3).

Benefits

Discretionary Annual Bonus: Subject to company and individual performance.
Comprehensive Benefits Package Including: Medical, dental and vision plans, 401k, generous PTO and paid company holidays, employee assistance program, flexible spending accounts, life insurance, disability coverage, learning & development programs and more!

Compensation

The salary range for this position considers a wide range of factors in making compensation decisions including but not limited to: Education, qualifications, skills, training, experience, certifications, internal equity, and location. jobs.title: Senior Real Estate & Facilities Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Overview Of Position

The Senior Real Estate & Facilities Analyst supports the Global Corporate Real Estate organization by transforming complex portfolio, financial, occupancy, lease, project, facilities, workplace, sustainability, and employee data into accurate reporting, actionable insights, and decision-support materials.

This role combines advanced analytics, data governance, business intelligence, technology enablement, and practical artificial intelligence capabilities with strong corporate real estate knowledge. The analyst develops dashboards, scorecards, forecasts, scenario models, business cases, and executive presentations that support portfolio optimization, workplace strategy, capital investment, lease decisions, operational improvement, and long-term planning.

The successful candidate is detail-oriented, technically capable, and able to communicate complex findings clearly to executive, financial, operational, and technical audiences while partnering effectively across functions and with external service providers.

What will be my duties and responsibilities in this job?

Data Analytics, Governance & Portfolio Analysis (25%)

Collect, cleanse, reconcile, validate, manipulate, and analyze structured and unstructured data from multiple internal and external systems.
Maintain data standards, definitions, ownership, validation procedures, business rules, quality controls, and documentation across Corporate Real Estate data sources.
Monitor data quality, identify discrepancies and root causes, and coordinate remediation with internal teams and external service providers.
Analyze occupancy cost, utilization, lease activity, facilities operations, capital projects, sustainability, workplace experience, employee work arrangements, and portfolio risk.
Develop key performance indicators, benchmarks, forecasts, trends, scenario models, and ad hoc analyses to support portfolio optimization, site consolidation, workplace strategy, lease decisions, and capital investment.

Business Intelligence, Reporting & Technology (25%)

Build, manage, and continuously enhance centralized dashboards, scorecards, reporting tools, and analytical platforms for site-level and consolidated portfolio reporting.
Translate business requirements into scalable data, reporting, visualization, and technology solutions using advanced Excel and business-intelligence tools.
Automate recurring data collection, validation, analysis, and reporting to reduce manual effort and improve the speed, consistency, and reliability of insights.
Support system integrations, data pipelines, interfaces, data warehousing, application programming interfaces, and connections between source systems and reporting platforms.
Maintain recurring Real Estate & Facilities metrics, balanced scorecards, capital budgeting, fixed-asset reporting, and operational reporting as required.

Artificial Intelligence & Innovation (20%)

Serve as a Corporate Real Estate resource for artificial intelligence, generative AI, intelligent automation, and emerging analytical technologies.
Identify, prioritize, test, and implement practical AI use cases for document analysis, lease abstraction, portfolio research, forecasting, data-quality monitoring, executive reporting, and employee-service delivery.
Partner with Technology, Information Security, Legal, Risk, and Data Governance teams to support responsible and policy-compliant AI adoption.
Develop user guidance, demonstrations, training materials, and adoption support while maintaining awareness of developments in AI, analytics, commercial real estate technology, and workplace intelligence.

Executive Reporting & Decision Support (20%)

Convert complex data and analysis into clear, concise business recommendations, dashboards, scorecards, business cases, and executive presentations.
Communicate portfolio performance, risks, trends, opportunities, business impact, and recommended actions through effective data visualization and storytelling.
Tailor reporting for executive, operational, financial, and technical audiences and support annual planning, quarterly reviews, leadership meetings, and strategic initiatives.

Stakeholder & Program Support (10%)

Partner with Real Estate, Facilities, Finance, Procurement, Human Resources, Technology, Risk, Sustainability, Security, and regional teams to define business questions, reporting requirements, and priorities.
Coordinate cross-functional analytics and technology initiatives, including plans, milestones, dependencies, risks, deliverables, adoption, and performance measures.
Maintain productive relationships with service providers, technology vendors, consultants, and data partners; support continuous improvement and other analyses identified by leadership.

What are the requirements needed for this position?

Education

Bachelor’s degree in data analytics, business analytics, information systems, computer science, finance, real estate, business administration, engineering, or a related field.

Professional Experience

Five or more years of progressive experience in data analytics, business intelligence, data governance, technology, corporate real estate, finance, or a related discipline.
Experience developing complex analyses, dashboards, reports, data-quality processes, or technology-enabled solutions using information from multiple systems.

Knowledge And Skills

Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including complex formulas, PivotTables, Power Query, data modeling, scenario analysis, charts, and large-dataset manipulation.
Experience developing dashboards and visualizations using Power BI, Tableau, or a comparable business-intelligence platform.
Understanding of data governance, data quality, master data, business definitions, controls, validation, and ownership.
Professional experience using artificial intelligence or generative AI tools and an understanding of responsible-use considerations.
Strong analytical, organizational, project-management, problem-solving, written, verbal, presentation, and executive-communication skills.
Ability to translate technical or analytical findings into clear business recommendations, manage multiple priorities independently, and collaborate across functions and organizational levels.

What other skills/experience would be helpful to have?

Masters degree in a relevant field.

Professional Experience

Experience supporting a geographically dispersed corporate real estate portfolio or working within a Fortune 500 company.
Knowledge of portfolio strategy, transactions, lease administration, occupancy planning, facilities management, capital projects, workplace experience, sustainability, financial modeling, forecasting, benchmarking, and scenario planning.
Experience with integrated workplace management systems, lease-administration platforms, facility-management systems, occupancy technologies, or corporate real estate databases.
Experience working with outsourced service providers, technology vendors, consultants, and cross-functional global teams.

Job Summary

The Information Security Analyst II supports and strengthens the university’s information security program by implementing, monitoring, and improving controls that protect institutional data, systems, and infrastructure. This role administers security configurations, investigates threats and incidents, conducts risk-based access reviews, and ensures alignment with applicable regulatory requirements and security standards. The analyst collaborates across IT and academic units to integrate security best practices into daily operations, communicates security requirements to technical and non-technical audiences, and supports ongoing security awareness and continuous improvement.

FGCU is building a culture of curiosity, commitment and collaboration. We value employees who successfully work with others and drive positive change through critical thinking and decisive action. If you thrive in an environment of innovation, accountability and mutual respect, you will find a good home here.

At Florida Gulf Coast University, employees are expected to work on campus as part of a collaborative, mission-driven environment. While this role does not directly interact with students, its on-site presence is essential to supporting the university’s operations and advancing student learning across the institution.

Job Description

Typical duties include but are not limited to:

Administers and maintains identity and access management (IAM) controls, including roles, permission sets, query and report access, component interfaces, and automated process groups, in alignment with least-privilege principles.
Designs and maintains security items such as roles, permission lists, query and report access, component interfaces, and batch process groups.
Detects, investigates, and resolves security events, policy violations, and anomalous activity; documents findings and escalates incidents in accordance with the university’s incident response procedures.
Identifies, reports, and resolves security violations.
Manages user provisioning and de-provisioning workflows, evaluates access requests against established role definitions, and troubleshoots authentication and authorization issues across enterprise platforms.
Administers security aspects for users, identifies appropriate security accesses, and troubleshoots security and access issues.
Partners with IT and academic units to assess security risks, drive process improvements, and ensure that security controls are effectively integrated into operational workflows and project delivery.
Collaborates with users to maintain and improve information security processes and procedures.
Maintains accurate security documentation, including asset records, acceptable use guidance, network security standards, and evidence artifacts required for audit and compliance purposes.
Maintains records, forms, and documents the proper use of the network.
Tracks and manages security-related work requests, incidents, and projects using the IT service management (ITSM) platform, ensuring timely resolution and accurate reporting.
Completes tracking in the work order system.
Conducts periodic access certification reviews and user entitlement audits to verify compliance with established security standards, FERPA, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and other applicable regulatory requirements.
Conducts access review audits to ensure compliance with established security standards and policy guidelines.
Designs and implements data protection controls, including encryption, data loss prevention (DLP) configurations, and secure data handling procedures to reduce exposure from unauthorized access or exfiltration.
Develops new techniques and procedures to protect data from unauthorized users.
Continuously evaluates security processes and tool effectiveness; develops recommendations for control improvements and promotes adoption of current security frameworks and industry best practices.
Reviews processes, evaluates results, recommends new processes, and promotes best practices.
Identifies capability gaps in the university’s security posture, develops business cases for security investments, and leads or contributes to implementation projects that advance institutional security objectives.
Identifies the need for functionalities that enhance the organization's security posture and manages projects to implement these enhancements.

Other Duties

Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

Additional Job Description

Required Qualifications:

This position requires either seven years of directly related full-time experience or, as an alternative, a Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in computer science, business administration, or related field and three years of full-time experience directly related to the job functions.
Professional full-time experience working with wide and local area networks, business applications development and support, systems security, or related experience.
Any appropriate combination of relevant education, experience, and/or certifications may be considered.

Preferred Qualifications

Three years full time professional experience working with wide and local area networks or business applications development and support.
Security specific certifications such as GIAC, CEH, or CISSP.
Experience working with CIS Critical Controls or NIST 800 series documents.
Experience working in Higher Education.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Proven ability to think strategically and approach challenges with creativity.
Demonstrated track record of reliability, meeting goals, and holding oneself accountable.
Strong interpersonal skills and experience working effectively across teams.
Knowledge of security strategies (operating system hardening, vulnerability management, change management, application testing/patching, security tools, and software products).Knowledge of modern security domains including endpoint and OS hardening, vulnerability and patch management, identity and access management, cloud security, application security testing, and security tooling (SIEM, EDR, DLP, IDS/IPS).
Knowledge of network/system security access, management, and testing.
Knowledge of network and system security principles, including segmentation, access control architectures, zero trust concepts, and security testing methodologies.
Knowledge of applicable security policies, best practices, and principles.
Knowledge of standard computer logging processes and understanding of the types of events logged.
Skill in identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.
Excellent interpersonal skills.
Advanced verbal and written communication skills and the ability to present effectively to small and large groups.
Ability to take initiative to plan, organize, coordinate and perform work in various situations when numerous and competing demands are involved.
Ability to collaborate and work effectively within the community and willing to contribute to a team effort.
Ability to work independently and follow through on assignments.
Ability to translate security concepts to all areas of the business.Ability to communicate security risk and technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences, including faculty, senior leadership, and end users.
Ability to interpret log data and investigate potential issues.Ability to analyze SIEM alerts, log data, and security telemetry to identify indicators of compromise, anomalous behavior, or emerging threats, and triage findings for investigation or escalation.
Ability to prepare network/system diagrams and advise on secure implementations of systems and services.Ability to develop network and system security architecture diagrams and provide guidance on secure design principles, configuration baselines, and hardening standards for infrastructure and cloud environments.
Ability to discern between security breaches and more innocent technical bugs.Ability to apply sound analytical judgment to differentiate genuine security incidents from false positives, technical misconfigurations, or benign anomalies, reducing alert fatigue and improving response quality.

Institutional Values & Behavioral Expectation

In this role, the successful candidate will be expected to:

Seek out new approaches to improve outcomes; remain open for feedback and new ideas.
Lead with integrity; consistently produce high-quality work; persevere to overcome obstacles to meet deadlines and achieve deliverables.
Share information and insights thoughtfully; build partnerships across departments; communicate respectfully; support colleagues to achieve common goals.
