Who We Are

Vident Advisory serves as a valued partner to asset managers and sponsors, offering portfolio management, trading, operational, and capital markets expertise across indexed and active strategies. We support ETFs, UCITS, mutual funds, SMAs, hedge funds, and other vehicles across global equity, fixed income, currency, commodity, and alternative markets, including strategies that utilize derivative instruments. Our platform enables clients to efficiently launch, operate, and scale investment strategies across multiple jurisdictions.

What You’ll Do

This role sits in the day-to-day fund operations function, supporting a wide range of asset classes and strategies with a strong emphasis on accurate, timely trade processing and settlement. Buy-side funds operations experience preferred. The Senior Portfolio Operations Analyst
is responsible for ensuring the integrity of daily data, accurate and timely post-trade booking, smooth settlement and reconciliation processes, margin/collateral management, and effective support to internal and external stakeholders across time zones. The role requires a solid understanding of investment operations across multiple asset classes and the systems that support them and takes on a greater degree of independent ownership and problem-solving than an entry-level analyst position. The position requires close collaboration within the team and across the organization, emphasizing teamwork, adaptability, and proactive communication.

Key Responsibilities

Start-of-Day (SOD) Controls and Data Validation
Perform daily SOD checks on pricing, reference data, curves, corporate actions, and other inputs supporting portfolios across asset classes.
Monitor automated data pipelines, investigate breaks or missing data, and re-run or escalate processes as needed to ensure accurate downstream reporting and valuation.

Trade Execution, Booking, and Cash Activity (Bloomberg AIM or comparable platform)
Oversee daily trade executions, matching, and booking of T+1 activity into the portfolio/accounting system, including creations/redemptions (cash and in-kind), custody FX trades, distributions, fees, and miscellaneous cash entries.
Ensure accurate reflection of position and cash impacts across systems and coordinate with custodians and fund accountants on discrepancies.

Margin, Collateral, and Corporate Actions
Manage daily margin calls and instruct associated collateral movements as needed.
Monitor corporate actions, submit elections and instructions as required, and verify post-event position and cash outcomes.

Reconciliations and Settlements
Perform daily position and cash reconciliations between internal systems, custodians, and fund accounting records.
Investigate and resolve reconciliation breaks related to pricing, accruals, FX, timing, or booking issues.
Support timely settlement of trades, following up on failed or delayed settlements with brokers and custodians.

Brokerage & Custodial Relationships
Maintain existing brokerage and custodial relationships and assist with new account onboardings.

Ongoing Operational Support
Assist with month-end and period-end processes, NAV support, portfolio reporting, and audit or regulatory data requests.
Help maintain and build technology to support investment trading and portfolio management, and contribute to process improvements, documentation, and control enhancements as product complexity grows.

Who You Are

M.B.A./Bachelor's degree in finance (or related major) required.
5+ years of experience in the investment management industry with a focus on nvestment operations across multiple asset classes, portfolio support, fund accounting, or middle/back office functions.
Candidates must be analytical, detail-oriented, and precise with numbers, with a solid understanding of securities/fund industry investment concepts and strategies, and the ability to trace data and cash flows across multiple systems.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and comfort working with operational data and reconciliations.
Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with internal teams and external counterparties across different time zones.

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Senior Data Analyst

Why join Housr?

We’re building Housr

to make life easier for students living off campus, from finding somewhere to live to accessing the services, offers and experiences around them.
We’ve reached $10m ARR and raised a $10m Series A to support our growth. As we expand across the UK and North America, we’re looking for a Senior Data Analyst to help us make better use of the data across our business.

The opportunity

We collect useful data across our product, sales, marketing and operations. The next step is turning more of it into clear answers that help teams decide what to do.
You’ll own analysis across the business, build reporting that people can use themselves, and investigate the questions that need a closer look. That could mean understanding why one student cohort is more engaged than another, where people drop out of a journey, or how acquisition costs compare with the value customers bring.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role, with regular contact across the business and leadership team, and has room to shape how we work with data.

Why this role is interesting

Our current setup includes MySQL, HubSpot, Google Analytics and Metabase. Some analysis can happen within those systems today; joining information across them still involves manual work.
We’re planning a more connected data platform. You’ll help define the questions it needs to answer, the metrics we should agree on and the reporting teams need, working with engineering and external specialists on the wider build. There’s plenty of useful analysis to get into while that work develops.

What you’ll own

Proactive analysis of product usage, cohorts, conversion, retention and commercial performance.
Clear recommendations that help Product, Sales, Marketing, Finance and Operations make decisions.
Dashboards and reporting that give teams a reliable view of their performance.
Shared definitions for important metrics, with clear documentation and checks on data quality.
Ad hoc investigations that explain what is happening, why it might be happening and what we should do next.
Practical ways to combine data from different sources, being clear about any gaps or limitations.
Support for colleagues to understand and use data in their day-to-day work and quarterly reviews.
Input into the future data warehouse, including reporting requirements, useful data models and consistent definitions.

What we’re looking for

You’ve taken analysis from an initial business question through to a recommendation that people acted on.
You’re confident using SQL to investigate relational data, join datasets and check your work.
You’ve built dashboards in Metabase or a comparable BI tool, and helped colleagues use them.
You understand product and commercial measures such as cohorts, conversion, retention, customer acquisition cost and lifetime value.
You can explain your findings clearly to people who don’t work in data, including where the evidence is incomplete.
You’re organised, careful with detail and comfortable deciding which questions deserve attention first.
You enjoy working across teams and can challenge an assumption or ask a difficult question constructively.

A real nice to have

Experience in a marketplace, consumer product, subscription business or growing technology company would be useful. 
Familiarity with HubSpot, Google Analytics or a warehouse project would also help. 
We’re open to someone already working at Senior level or an experienced analyst ready for broader ownership.

What we offer

Genuine competitive salary with full details closed at initial interview
25 days’ holiday plus bank holidays.
Amazing Central Manchester office with great transport links
Monthly team lunches, a monthly afternoon for personal development or time for yourself, and company socials.
The chance to shape how a growing business uses data, with direct access to the teams acting on your work.

Interview process

We aim to keep the process straightforward and relevant to the role.
An introductory conversation with our Talent Partner.
A conversation with Nick, our COO, about your experience and the work ahead.
A practical data analysis task and discussion, with the brief and time commitment shared in advance.
A final conversation with our leadership team.

We’re happy to discuss any adjustments that would help you take part in the process.

We bridge strategy and execution, partnering with People leadership and cross-functional teams across Finance, Legal, and the business to turn ambiguous problems into durable programs.

What you’ll do

We’re looking for a collaborative, action-oriented Project Manager to join the Total Rewards Strategy and Enablement team. In this role, you’ll lead business-critical People projects, with a primary focus on mergers and acquisitions (M&A).

Bringing an acquired business into Stripe requires coordinated work across Total Rewards, People Partners, Recruiting, People Operations, Legal, Finance, and Corporate Development. You’ll project manage the People workstream from diligence and integration planning through close and post-close execution. You’ll turn deal-specific decisions into clear plans, ownership, milestones, and risk-management approaches.

You’ll coordinate functional owners across People workstreams, establish plans and dependencies, and step into the work when needed to unblock progress or close critical gaps. Your work will support transaction timelines, reduce business disruption, and create a consistent experience for acquired Stripes.

You’ll build People M&A’s capabilities through repeatable playbooks, infrastructure, and cross-training. This individual contributor role is well suited to someone who can bring structure to ambiguity and move between strategy and execution.

Responsibilities

Project manage People M&A workstreams from diligence and planning through close and post-close execution. Workstreams may include organizational alignment, employee data, onboarding, recruiting, and people program integration.
Serve as a central coordination point across Total Rewards, People Partners, People Operations, People Systems, Recruiting, People Support, Corporate Development, Legal, Finance, and Corporate Technology.
Align plans, dependencies, decisions, and accountability with transaction timelines.
Develop and run integration and change-management plans that give functional leads, acquired Stripes, and other affected audiences the information and support they need at each stage of a transaction.
Identify cross-functional dependencies, risks, and blockers early. Coordinate resolution and escalate issues when needed to protect integration timelines and the Stripe experience.
Establish feedback and support mechanisms for acquired Stripes, including surveys, office hours, and centralized support channels. Use feedback to improve integration plans and change-management approaches.
Build and improve People M&A’s infrastructure, including project plans, templates, checklists, playbooks, reporting, and retrospective documentation.
Build capability across People workstreams through documentation, cross-training, and shared practices that support more consistent future integrations.
Support other business-critical and transformational projects across Total Rewards and the People team as needed.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

You have 7+ years of project or program management experience at a global company, including 2+ years project managing workstreams within the M&A lifecycle, including diligence, integration planning, close readiness, and post-close integration.
You have experience leading complex, cross-functional programs from planning through execution and building repeatable program infrastructure, such as integration playbooks, project-plan templates, readiness checklists, risk logs, or retrospective processes.
You have a track record of turning ambiguous problems into structured, repeatable programs. You’re comfortable building new programs in a scaling environment while improving and standardizing how work gets done.
You have excellent written and verbal communication skills. You can write a one-page executive update, a decision memo tailored to stakeholders, and a step-by-step operator playbook with equal fluency. You guide project teams through complex work in a direct, approachable, and inclusive way.
You can manage senior cross-functional stakeholders across Total Rewards, People Partners, People Systems, Recruiting, Corporate Development, Legal, and Finance. You know when to build alignment, raise a risk, and escalate.
You’re comfortable working with data and systems such as Workday and Greenhouse. You use data to clarify decisions, communicate recommendations, and define requirements with People Systems partners.
You focus on the experience of acquired Stripes and the teams operating the program, not only on program artifacts.
You can manage competing priorities and adapt in a fast-paced environment. You work effectively independently and across teams, bring structure to complexity, and follow through on the details that make a program successful.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with change management frameworks, such as the Prosci ADKAR Model, and applying them to employee or operational change.
Project or program management certification or training, such as Project Management Professional (PMP), Lean, Six Sigma, or a comparable methodology

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $127,600 - $191,400. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

About the Opportunity

Our client is a leading energy organization seeking an experienced Project Manager to support the development of large-scale natural gas power generation facilities across the United States.

This individual will work closely with Lead Project Managers, engineering teams, and other key stakeholders to help move projects through early-stage development, permitting, technical assessments, and construction readiness. The role will focus heavily on identifying project risks, coordinating across multiple teams, and ensuring projects remain aligned with cost, schedule, and development milestones.

The ideal candidate has direct experience working on natural gas-fired power plants that generate electricity for the grid, specifically simple-cycle or combined-cycle facilities. While a strong understanding of power generation systems is important, this is a project management position rather than a hands-on engineering design role.

Key Responsibilities

Support early-stage development of natural gas power generation projects, including due diligence, preliminary engineering, permitting, and construction readiness.

Identify, assess, and mitigate risks related to project scope, cost, schedule, permitting, and technical requirements.
Monitor project budgets, schedules, milestones, and overall progress, identifying potential delays or cost impacts.

Experience supporting early-stage project development, including planning, due diligence, permitting, or construction readiness.
Demonstrated experience managing project risks, costs, schedules, and milestones.

Proactive, collaborative working style and the ability to independently manage priorities in a remote environment.

Experience supporting gas power generation projects from early development through construction or execution.
Background working with utility owners, power generation developers, or EPC contractors.
Familiarity with gas and electrical interconnections, balance-of-plant systems, and permitting requirements.
Experience supporting major equipment procurement, contractor bid evaluations, and project cost estimates.
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience considered.

This is an opportunity to support major natural gas power generation projects during critical early development phases. The Project Manager will work alongside experienced power generation professionals while gaining exposure to engineering, project controls, permitting, EPC contracting, and construction planning.

The position offers a remote work environment, collaboration across multiple disciplines, and the opportunity to contribute to large-scale energy infrastructure projects.

Job Description

WSP is seeking a Power Delivery Senior Project Manager
for our Power & Energy Power Delivery Management Team.

The Senior Project Manager (SPM) is responsible for managing the day-to-day activities of the project management team to produce a product consistent with WSP mission statement and our culture.The SPMis expected to lead by example in adhering to WSP's culture and defined project management and business practices and to achieve the goals of the business plan, maintain WSP's high-quality standards, promote internal teamwork and meet the needs of our clients. The successful candidate may work from a mutually acceptable location within the United States and will be based out of any WSP local office with the ability to work remotely in a hybrid office arrangement. You must have the ability to travel to a WSP and/or Client office for periodic in-person meetings.

This Opportunity

The SPM provides technical, administrative, and commercial project management leadership and project management oversight for the development, execution, delivery, management, control and monitoring of Substation, Transmission and Distribution Line projects throughout the US in support of company, regional, and national business line goals. This position will focus on managing engineering projects for Engineer, Procure, Construction (EPC) clients.Ensures all responsibilities throughout the full project lifecycle including proposal phase, planning and project startup, project execution, procurement, construction support, schedule, cost control, reporting, and project closeout are executed, adhered to, delivered, and audited with a level of quality that meets or exceeds corporate and client project excellence and delivery standards. Provide engineering team guidance on providing engineering solutions that not only meet codes and standards but also provide total installed value to the client and ultimate owner/operator of the facility.

Your Impact

Provide Project Management leadership for all small/medium/large scale/more complex high voltage and EHV projects throughout the US including pursuit and development of opportunities, initiation, planning, execution, controlling, and closing, ensuring support for preparing and overseeing project detailed design, budgets, forecasts, margins and KPIs, monitoring external events and risk contingencies, ensuring satisfactory performance, and managing the contractual obligations to deliver the project or assigned portfolio of assigned project(s) as defined in the contract and client’s expectations.

Facilitate and lead project kick ‑ off, safety, and execution alignment meetings with key internal and external stakeholders to establish roles, responsibilities, and delivery expectations.
Coordinate with area managers, technical leads, and resource managers to address staffing, subcontracting, and specialty support needs in a timely manner .
Maintain regular client communications, including monthly progress reporting, safety performance, major risks/issues, and scope or budget impacts, reinforcing WSP’s role as a trusted advisor .
Participate in and oversee problem project reviews, providing input about root cause issues and potential solutions. Assist with developing project recovery plans.
Ensure regular project reporting and updates are provided to clients, technical areas, and business unit managers, identifying any emergent issues with scope, risk, and/or budget.
Monitor and manage accounts receivable (AR), unbilled revenue, cash flow, and invoicing, coordinating with project accounting and finance teams to resolve issues and maintain financial health of projects.
Complete formal project closeout activities, including financial closeout, documentation archiving, client acceptance, and lessons ‑ learned workshops to support continuous improvement .
Collaborate with cross ‑ disciplinary professionals to deliver integrated, future ‑ ready power delivery solutions, strengthening WSP’s position as a trusted advisor to clients .
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Develop new and existing clients and seek opportunities for Division growth.
Ensure EPC clients and ultimate owner/operators of the facility expectations are met and/or exceeded.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

15+ years of relevant post education experience in a project management role within the Power Delivery/Utility Industry.

Minimum of 5 years of experience leading engineering and/or construction teams on medium to large electrical utility scale clients for medium, high voltage and/or extra high voltage power delivery type projects.

Advanced-level understanding of project delivery process, specifically EPC delivery model, within the Power Delivery/Utility industry and strong background and experience in project management.
Advanced proficiency with analytical and organizational skills, with business acumen to bridge the business and project management.
Advanced proficiency with critical thinking, risk ‑ based decision ‑ making, and problem-solving skills to make assessments and calculations involving the application of project management principles, with a sound understanding of intent, impact, and optimize project outcomes.
Advanced proficiency with interpersonal and communication skills to interact effectively, persuasively, and tactfully with leadership, clients, subcontractors, consultants, and internal teams .

Position

About the role

Apellix is hiring a Drone LMS Project Manager (Apellix Academy Manager) to own the online training program every new operator must pass before their drone leaves our warehouse.

Apellix builds semi-autonomous drones for power washing, soft washing, spray painting, coatings and NDT inspection. Our drones are 100% U.S.-made, NDAA-compliant, U.S. Army-certified, and flying in 21 countries.

You will run Apellix Academy end to end: building new modules, keeping existing ones current as our products and software change, enrolling and tracking learners, and making sure every buyer is ready for hands-on training. This is a role for someone who has already built drone training content inside an LMS and wants to own a program, not just contribute to one.

What you'll do

Build new content

Design and produce new Academy modules for each platform (B2, Blue, SPD, SPD Blue, NDT).
Write scripts, storyboards, quizzes and assessments; shoot and edit video, screen recordings and walkthroughs with our engineering and production teams.
Turn technical material from engineers into clear, practical lessons for non-aviator operators.

Maintain and improve the program

Edit and update existing modules whenever hardware, firmware, software or procedures change, and retire outdated content.
Use completion rates, quiz results and trainer feedback to find where learners struggle, then fix those lessons.
Keep Academy content aligned with hands-on training in Jacksonville and on-site trainer visits.
Coordinate with partner-delivered content, such as our "how to clean" course, so learners get one consistent experience.

Run the LMS

Administer the LMS: enroll buyers and operators, set up courses and learning paths, manage roles, permissions and certificates.
Track each learner's progress and confirm Academy completion, since no drone ships until the pilot completes the Academy and hands-on training.
Answer learner questions and nudge buyers who stall so they can schedule hands-on training sooner.
Report regularly on enrollments, completion times and pass rates.

Grow the Academy

Recommend new courses, certifications or tiers (e.g., refresher, advanced, or international versions) that improve operator results.
Help evaluate LMS tools and integrations, including connections to our customer portal.

Required qualifications

FAA Part 107 License.
Drone training content built in an LMS (required).
You have designed, produced and published drone or UAS training courses on an LMS such as TalentLMS, Thinkific, LearnDash, Docebo, Moodle or similar. Please share samples or links.
3+ years in instructional design, e-learning development or technical training.
Hands-on LMS administration: enrollments, learning paths, assessments, certificates and reporting.
Comfort with authoring and media tools to produce video, interactive and quiz content yourself.
Ability to learn complex hardware and software quickly and explain it plainly to people new to industrial drones.
Strong writing and organization; you can run a program with minimal oversight.

Nice to have

Experience with industrial, commercial or enterprise drone platforms (spraying, cleaning, inspection) rather than only consumer drones.
Background in the power washing, coatings or field-services trades.
Experience training a customer base (not just employees), including international learners; Spanish a plus.

Benefits

Federal holidays
401(k) and company contributions
Paid healthcare with Telehealth and counseling 

To apply:
send your resume and links to at least two drone training modules or courses you built in an LMS.

jobs.title: Senior Implementation Manager - Treasury Safeguarding
jobs.description:
Company Description

Wise is a global technology company, building the best way to move and manage the world’s money.

Min fees. Max ease. Full speed.

Whether people and businesses are sending money to another country, spending abroad, or making and receiving international payments, Wise is on a mission to make their lives easier and save them money.

As part of our team, you will be helping us create an entirely new network for the world's money.

For everyone, everywhere.

Job Description

More about our mission
and what we offer
.

We're looking for an Implementation Manager to join our fast-growing Finance & Treasury Product team in London or Tallinn. This is a unique opportunity to have an impact on Wise's mission by making sure our customers' money stays safe as we launch new products and expand into new markets.

Your mission

Wise customers trust us to keep their money safe. Safeguarding is how we make sure that every penny we hold for customers is protected, in every country we operate in.

Today we run safeguarding across 11 legal entities and client asset protection (CASS) across 6. That means more than 500 bank accounts in scope, 5+ external audits a year, regular internal audit and regulator reviews, and several new legal entities launching every year.

As Wise grows, so does our Safeguarding team. Our global team builds and runs the automated controls and tools that every entity relies on, while regional teams own what happens locally. As the Implementation Manager, you'll connect the two. You'll make sure new products and entities are onboarded into our controls properly, and that incidents are handled quickly and transparently.

You'll work closely with the Safeguarding Product Manager, Safeguarding Engineering and Analytics, Treasury and Regulatory Product Compliance, Finance, Payment and Treasury Operations, and regional controllers around the world.

How You'll Contribute To Our Mission

New product reviews, onboarding and approval

Run the safeguarding review and approval process for new products and product changes, making sure every step is followed and nothing launches without the right controls in place.
Follow up with product teams, Treasury Regulatory Product Compliance and Finance to keep projects moving.
Keep a clear, up-to-date tracker of projects that need safeguarding support, and report on their status.

New entity launches

Support new legal entities as they launch, working out how they'll be onboarded into our global systems and controls.
Define how controls need to be set up locally for each entity, for example safeguarding timings.
Work with Regional Finance and Compliance so that local controllers are ready to take ownership from day one.

Execution and implementation

Plan and lead the work to integrate new Wise products into our safeguarding systems, together with product managers, engineers, data analysts and operations specialists.
Own large, complex integrations from start to finish, and support the team with clear documentation: requirements, project plans, resourcing, testing and delivery.

Support

Keep documentation of product flows and safeguarding calculations up to date.
Get hands-on when things go wrong: help product and engineering teams understand the impact of an incident, drive it to resolution, and improve controls so it doesn't happen again.

Qualifications

A bit about you

You know regulated finance. You have experience in implementation, controls, regulatory operations or treasury operations in financial services or fintech, and you're used to working alongside Compliance to launch things the right way.
You understand how customer money is protected. You know safeguarding, client money/CASS or a similar framework for protecting customer funds. If you know one regime well and are keen to learn others, that works too.
You enjoy getting deep into the processing logic. You're comfortable with reconciliations, ledgers and financial data. You like to understand in depth how money flows through a product and what it depends on, and you can explain what a reconciliation break means and why it matters.
You create clarity. You bring people together behind a common goal, balance different points of view and bring structure to complex problems. You write clearly, and you can explain complex concepts in simple terms to engineers, compliance specialists, finance teams and senior stakeholders without losing the nuance.
You get it done. You keep many workstreams moving across teams and time zones without losing track of the details. You hold others to account without being their line manager, and you follow things through to the end.
You stay calm when things go wrong. You make sound calls during incidents, and you know when to escalate.

Some Extra Skills That Are Great (but Not Essential)

Experience supporting external or internal audits, or regulator inspections.
Experience with control frameworks, obligation-to-control mapping or risk tools.
Working knowledge of SQL or data tools (e.g. Looker, Snowflake) for investigating issues yourself.
Experience launching a new regulated entity or a new market.
Familiarity with safeguarding rules in more than one region (UK, EU, APAC, North America).

Additional Information

For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive.

We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences.

Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers.

If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs.

Keep up to date with life at Wise by following us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

Responsibilities

IT Project Manager- Infrastructure/ Security

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0tMgKm_71qs

Meet the Recruiter:
Amber Smallwood

What You'll Get To Do

We are seeking an experienced IT Project Manager to lead and support a portfolio of enterprise infrastructure, cybersecurity, cloud, network, data center, and business technology transformation initiatives. The ideal candidate will possess a strong background in project management, IT infrastructure, and information security programs, with a proven ability to successfully deliver complex, cross-functional projects from initiation through deployment and operational transition.

This role will partner closely with Infrastructure, Information Security, Enterprise Architecture, Network Operations, Cloud Engineering, End User Services, business stakeholders, external vendors, and executive leadership to ensure the successful execution of strategic technology initiatives.

The successful candidate will report directly to the IT Project Manager- Infrastructure/ Security
and will operate in a remote environment while leading geographically dispersed project teams, vendors, and stakeholders. The role requires strong leadership, communication, risk management, and governance capabilities, along with the ability to drive alignment across technical and business organizations.

Candidates with prior experience leading large-scale infrastructure deployments, IT Security programs, cloud transformation initiatives, network and data center projects, IT operational improvements, technology modernization efforts, and PMO governance activities are highly desired. Experience working within regulated environments and managing projects involving security, compliance, business continuity, and disaster recovery requirements is a plus.

Business Relationship / IT Project Management

Foster strong partnerships with customers, stakeholders, and sponsors.
Develop and maintain project plans, schedules, budgets, resource forecasts, and status reporting.
Lead project execution through all phases of the project lifecycle, including initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, and closure.
Partner with technical leads, architects, cybersecurity professionals, and service owners to establish delivery plans, manage dependencies, coordinate technical reviews, and ensure required architecture, security, and operational approvals are completed.
Ensure projects are delivered on time, within scope, and within budget.
Facilitate project governance, steering committee meetings, and executive status reviews.

IT Governance

Ensure that all organizational governance, compliance, security, and change control needs are met.
Provide weekly reports to organizational and Sponsor management highlighting issues and escalations needed.
Support testing, cutover planning, deployment readiness, and stabilization activities.

Stakeholder Management

Build strong relationships with business leaders, IT teams, consultants, and vendors.
Provide clear, concise communication to project teams and executive stakeholders.
Facilitate decision-making and drive issue resolution.
Manage stakeholder expectations and project communications.

Risk, Financial & Resource Management

Identify project risks, issues, assumptions, and dependencies.
Develop mitigation and contingency plans.
Track project financials, forecasts, budgets, and resource allocations.
Monitor project performance using established PMO methodologies and governance standards.

Change Management & Adoption

Partner with business stakeholders to support organizational change management activities.
Coordinate training, communications, and transition planning.
Assist with business readiness efforts to ensure successful adoption of new processes and systems.

Qualifications

What You'll Bring:

Education & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
8+ years of progressive IT experience, with exposure to enterprise infrastructure, cybersecurity, cloud services, network, data center, endpoint, or related technology environments.
Minimum of 5 years of project management experience delivering enterprise infrastructure, IT Security, cloud, network, data center, or end-user technology initiatives.
Experience in a broad scope of IT technologies including cloud-based solutions such as IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS.
Strong understanding of project management methodologies including Waterfall, Agile, and hybrid approaches.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting infrastructure separation, integration, consolidation, or migration activities associated with mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, organizational restructuring, or site transitions.
Previous PMO, portfolio management, or governance experience.
PMP will be considered a primary preferred project management certification with Agile/Scrum as secondary certification.
Experience with ServiceNow SPM, Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or similar project management tools.

Desired Candidate Profile

The Ideal Candidate Will Bring a Blend Of

Strong project management discipline and leadership.
Ability to influence and persuade business management in the areas of developing sound and practical IT solutions.
Executive presence and the ability to influence across all organizational levels.
Proven success delivering large-scale business and technology transformation initiatives.
Ability to work independently in a highly collaborative remote environment.

Success Measures

In this role, the IT Project Manager will be expected to:

Maintain project schedules, financials, and governance artifacts with high accuracy.
Proactively identify and mitigate project risks.
Provide clear executive-level reporting and communication.
Enable successful business adoption of implemented solutions.
Contribute to PMO governance, best practices, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Benefits & Perks - What's In It For You

Panasonic prioritizes total well-being and offers comprehensive benefits options to support physical, emotional, financial, social, and environmental health:

Health Benefits – Offering medical, dental, vision, prescription plans, plus Health Savings Account and Flexible Spending Account options.
Voluntary Benefits – Life, accident, critical illness, disability, legal, identity theft, and pet insurance.

Available to eligible employees starting the first day of the month following your start date. Eligibility for each benefit may vary based on employment status, location, and length of service.
Employee Recognition Program - High5 employee recognition and awards platform, quarterly and annual employee recognition
Annual Bonus Program - Opportunity for an annual performance-based bonus.

We Take Opportunity Seriously

At Panasonic, we are committed to a workplace that genuinely fosters inclusion and belonging. Fairness and Honesty have been part of our core values for more than 100 years and we are proud of our diverse culture as an equal opportunity employer.

The wage range of $140,000 - $150,000 is just one component of Panasonic’s total package. Actual compensation varies depending on the individual’s knowledge, skills, experience, and location. This role may be eligible for discretionary bonuses and incentives.

Customer-centric: you keep business-unit outcomes and leadership decisions—not vendor outputs—as the success measure.

Pragmatic and persistent: you create clarity where none exists and close follow-up loops before they become escalations.

5+ years of programme or project management in technology, with cross-functional reach across product, engineering, and operations.
Product management or product-owner experience for technical or data products—someone who has shipped a v1 of something internal, not just managed a backlog.
Vendor coordination experience with major enterprise technology partners (e.g. hyperscalers, large system integrators).
Working understanding of AI, data engineering, or cloud architecture at a level sufficient to translate technical constraints into delivery plans and product decisions.

Lead-PM/PdM role on a Board-visible AI infrastructure programme sponsored by OCTO leadership.
Ownership of the enterprise AI telemetry product—Pearson's first enterprise view of "what AI is doing for us".
Direct collaboration with engineering, security, and business-unit leaders across Pearson, and visibility across OCTO and the Chief Data & AI Office.

At Pearson, we don't just build careers—we accelerate them. This position provides visibility across the Office of the Chief Technology Officer and the AI C4E, with a clear path into broader technical and strategic roles.

Join Us in Shaping the Future of Rail Infrastructure

Are you an experienced project manager with a strong background in rail or complex transport infrastructure? Join Tetra Tech and take ownership of high-profile projects that support the future of rail across the UK and Republic of Ireland.

You will work with clients, technical specialists, delivery partners and stakeholders to lead projects from early development through design, consents, delivery and handover. As Senior Project Manager, you will lead complex rail projects or substantial project workstreams through the full project lifecycle, establishing and managing the project scope, delivery strategy, baseline programme, resources, budget and reporting arrangements. You will also promote safe design and delivery in line with applicable UK or Irish duties, project assurance requirements and site arrangements.

Your Impact in This Position

Your leadership will help ensure that complex rail projects are delivered safely, efficiently and to the required quality, programme and commercial outcomes. You will provide clear direction to multidisciplinary project teams, build effective relationships with clients, operators, infrastructure managers, contractors and statutory bodies, and resolve technical, organisational and delivery interfaces before they affect project outcomes. You will maintain strong control of programme, cost, risk, change and resources, lead client meetings, provide accurate and concise progress reporting, escalate decisions at an early stage, and maintain clear records of commitments, actions and change. You will also support the development of bids and fee proposals, while mentoring project managers and assistant project managers and contributing to the growth of project delivery capability across the business.

Project Leadership and Delivery

Lead complex rail or transport infrastructure projects from early development through design, consents, delivery and handover, ensuring that scope, programme, resources and budgets remain under control.

Direct and coordinate technical teams across rail systems, civil and structural engineering, stations, depots, environment and stakeholder interfaces.

Risk, Change and Commercial Management

Manage risk, opportunity, issue and decision registers, while overseeing change, forecasting outturns and applying sound commercial judgement to protect project outcomes.

Stakeholder and Client Leadership

Communicate technical and project information clearly to senior stakeholders. Lead client meetings, manage relationships and resolve interfaces with operators, infrastructure managers, contractors and statutory bodies.

Safety, Assurance and Team Development

Promote safe design and delivery, coordinate assurance and approvals, support bids and fee proposals, and mentor project managers and assistant project managers.

Essential

Qualifications & Experience

Substantial experience managing rail or similarly complex transport infrastructure projects.
Experience working across multidisciplinary design and delivery interfaces.
Demonstrable experience managing programme, cost, risk, change and client relationships.
Sound commercial judgement and experience forecasting project outcomes.
Proven ability to lead project teams and communicate technical matters clearly to senior stakeholders.

Experience working with Network Rail, Transport for London, Iarnród Éireann, Transport Infrastructure Ireland or other rail authorities.

Experience of supporting bids, fee proposals and the development of less experienced project managers.

This opportunity offers a unique blend of project leadership, client engagement, and market development, supporting some of the region's most significant energy infrastructure initiatives. The successful candidate will leverage technical expertise, strong business acumen, and collaborative leadership skills to drive project success, develop strategic client partnerships, and contribute to the continued growth of WSP's Power & Delivery division.

Your Impact

Work with multidisciplinary engineering teams through the planning, design, review, and execution of large-scale transmission, substation and/or distribution projects.
Lead and grow the Transmission and Distribution practice.
Ensure engineering deliverables meet quality expectations, client requirements, and applicable regulatory standards.
Work closely with project controls to develop and monitor the cash flow andforecast as well as the project financial dashboard.
Coordinate technical interfaces between stakeholders, EPC contractors, consultants, vendors, and internal project teams.
Monitor engineering performance, schedules, budgets, and project milestones to support effective project delivery.
Identify, assess, and mitigate technical risks while fostering a proactive problem-solving culture.
Support procurement activities through technical reviews, bid evaluations, and contractor submissions.
Contribute to the development of engineering best practices and continuous improvement initiatives across the organization.
Make recommendations and be involved with important decision-making on highly technical and complex aspects of WSP projects.
Lead certain client accounts and engagements within T&D.
Support the growth of technical disciplines required for T&D.
Ensure compliance with all relevant regulations and standards and provide oversight and governance on the various major project ongoing within the T&D team.
Collaborate with other internal departments and stakeholders to improve quality and project delivery, including management of subconsultants.
Mentor and coach other T&D staff as required.

Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Civil, Structural, or a related Engineering discipline.
Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) designation in Canada or Ing. designation in Quebec is preferred. Candidates must be eligible for registration with the applicable provincial engineering regulatory body.
7+ years of progressive engineering and infrastructure project delivery experience.
Demonstrated success leading multidisciplinary engineering teams on utility, transmission, energy, or large infrastructure projects.
Strong knowledge of transmission line, substation, and power system engineering projects.
Experience overseeing engineering consultants, EPC contractors, vendors, and technical stakeholders.
Proven ability to manage technical risk, engineering quality processes, and complex project interfaces.
Exceptional communication, stakeholder engagement, commercial awareness, and leadership capabilities.

Why choose WSP?

We exist to shape communities to advance humanity. The brightest engineers, advisors and scientists from across the globe call WSP home.

Proudly Canadian – we are a Top 100 Employer in Canada for 2026
A global community of brilliant minds – your next idea, mentor, or opportunity is always within reach.
Limitless opportunities start here. Whether it’s across the country or around the globe, we’ll help you tailor your role to match your ambition—because your growth drives ours.
Flexible work, real balance – we recognize the importance of balance in our lives and encourage you to prioritize the balance in yours.

#WeAreWSP

AB, BC, NT, NU, SK & YK:
$104,100 – $138,000

MB & ON:
$95,000 – $130,800

NB, NL, NS, PEI & QC:
$94,100 – $124,900

The final salary awarded for this role may vary from the above range based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs. The wage range provided in this job posting may be subject to change for business purposes.

Make Your Mark

If you're driven by purpose and impact, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now and take the first step toward a rewarding career with us.

About Us

At WSP
, we exist to shape communities to advance humanity.

It’s why we bring people together who are wired to solve complex challenges - engineers, scientists, advisors, and technical experts who are driven by a common passion - to redefine what’s possible and shape what comes next. We are Visioneers.

As one of the world’s leading professional services firms, we partner with clients across transportation, infrastructure, environment, buildings, energy, water, mining and metals. We pair deep local knowledge with global insights to pioneer solutions designed to leave a lasting, positive impact.

At WSP
, you’ll join a community of brilliant minds that push boundaries every day - applying deep expertise and fuelling innovation to help create a more connected and resilient future. Here, your ideas are valued, your growth is supported, and you are encouraged to bring your authentic self to work. We empower our people to collaborate across disciplines, challenge the status quo, and shape a career with purpose.

Join us.

About Us

Our leading SaaS-based Global Employment Platform™ enables clients to expand into over 180 countries quickly and efficiently, without the complexities of establishing local entities. At G-P, we’re dedicated to breaking down barriers to global business and creating opportunities for everyone, everywhere.

Our diverse, remote-first teams are essential to our success. We empower our Dream Team members with flexibility and resources, fostering an environment where innovation thrives and every contribution is valued and celebrated.

The work you do here will positively impact lives around the world. We stand by our promise: Opportunity Made Possible. In addition to competitive compensation and benefits, we invite you to join us in expanding your skills and helping to reshape the future of work.

At G-P, we assist organizations in building exceptional global teams in days, not months—streamlining the hiring, onboarding, and management process to unlock growth potential for all.

About The Position

The Principal Product Program Manager is a systems-thinker who translates ambitious company goals into a highly structured "System View" to drive major outcomes. You will be the engine of execution. You will operationalize frameworks on the ground, manage complex concurrent programs, and lead execution to ensure timely delivery of outcomes. Crucially, as we scale our AI initiatives, this role demands a forward-thinking leader who actively leverages AI and Agentic workflows in their daily program architecture and successfully navigates the unique pacing and unpredictability of AI-driven development.

What You’ll Do

Manage multiple concurrent programs varying in size and complexity, maintaining objective oversight while demonstrating a deep passion for the program's success.
Ensure every program aligns to a strict Program Playbook—meaning the technical capability is successfully delivered and the targeted outcomes are fully realized.
Establish a consistent execution rhythm and rituals to force decision-making, remove blockers, and clarify ownership.
Act as an "information radiator," utilizing clear reporting systems to communicate delivery health, milestone tracking, and look-ahead risk analysis to leadership.
Integrate AI seamlessly into your program management workflows, such as utilizing AI and agentic tools to automate RAID (Risks, Actions, Issues, Decisions) logs and synthesize status updates into concise executive summaries.
Govern the inherent unpredictability of AI development, adapting traditional program management to account for experimentation.
Maintain a centralized Work Surface (e.g., Jira, Confluence) as the ultimate hub for tracking initiative status, critical paths, and dependencies.
Identify and overcome delivery roadblocks in a complex environment, escalating risks quickly and effectively.

Minimum Requirements

What We're Looking For:

Minimum of 7 years of experience in SaaS product development, program management, and release management.
Direct experience with AI-driven development lifecycles and utilizing AI/Agentic workflows to optimize program management architectures.
BS in Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, or a related technical field.
Proven ability to earn trust quickly, mobilize teams, and set direction in highly ambiguous environments.
Ability to deliver tough messages with grace, resolve conflict, and adapt to change rapidly.
Experience and familiarity with industry-standard project management software (e.g., Jira, Confluence, Google Suite).

Preferred Requirements

Deep proficiency in the rapidly evolving AI landscape (LLMs, generative AI, agentic frameworks) with a demonstrated ability to integrate these capabilities into practical, future-proof program management strategies.
Effective presenter, negotiator, and collaborator who can communicate with clarity and precision at all levels of the organization.
A strategic mindset equally passionate about business outcomes and deep technology.

The annual gross base salary range for this position is £82,000 - £102,000 plus variable compensation.

Our ranges are established using objective market benchmarking data for this level of work. Final placement within the range is determined by gender-neutral criteria, including the candidate's relevant skills, experience, and specific qualifications for the role.

Actual compensation for this position may vary and will depend on multiple factors such as relevant qualifications, experience, education, and geographic location. For Full-Time Regular Employees, this position is also eligible for additional compensation as follows:

Sales Roles: This position is eligible for a commission structure in addition to base salary.
Non-Sales Roles: This position is eligible for an annual bonus which is paid dependent on various factors, including and without limitation, individual and company performance in addition to base salary.

Benefits

G-P values its employees and offers excellent benefits and perks including generous paid parental leave, flexible time off, spending accounts, medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, sabbatical after 5 years and more.

Individuals residing, or applying to work, in the United States: California or Philadelphia

new_jobs.description:
UTA seeks a Senior Technical Program Manager to lead complex, cross-functional technology programs that support UTA’s rapidly evolving business. In this role, you will partner with senior stakeholders across Technology, Product, Finance, and Operations to deliver large-scale initiatives that drive efficiency, scale, and innovation across the agency. The ideal candidate brings deep program management expertise, strong technical fluency, and a proven ability to operate in ambiguity while influencing both engineering teams and executive leadership.

The salary range for this role is $160,000 to $190,000, commensurate with experience and skills.

What You Will Do

Lead the end-to-end planning and execution of large-scale, multi-phase technology programs, ensuring alignment with strategic business goals and on-time delivery.
Partner with engineering, product, and business leaders to define scope, success criteria, and program roadmaps across multiple workstreams.
Establish and drive program governance, including status reporting, dependency and risk tracking, and stakeholder communication.
Proactively identify and resolve cross-team dependencies, ensuring accountability, alignment, and efficient decision-making across business units.
Translate complex technical concepts and trade-offs into clear business impacts and recommendations for non-technical stakeholders.
Anticipate, surface, and mitigate risks, escalating when needed while driving solutions independently and decisively.
Define, track, and communicate key program metrics to measure progress, velocity, quality, and outcomes.
Provide clear, executive-ready communication and reporting to senior and C-level stakeholders.
Roll up your sleeves when necessary—diving into technical details, clarifying requirements, and removing blockers to maintain momentum.

What You Will Need

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.
8+ years of experience in program or project management, including at least 4 years in a dedicated Technical Program Manager role.
Strong technical background with the ability to understand system architecture, data flows, integration patterns, and engineering trade-offs.
Proven track record delivering large, cross-functional initiatives in fast-paced, dynamic environments.
Demonstrated experience working closely with software engineering and product teams; familiarity with SDLC, Agile methodologies, and modern collaboration/tooling.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence and drive alignment at all levels of the organization, including executives.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with comfort using data and metrics to inform decisions and prioritize work.
Bias for action and ownership; operates as a driver of outcomes rather than a coordinator of tasks.
Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and modern data systems (e.g., Snowflake, Databricks, Kafka).
Ability to present to executive audiences with clarity and confidence, tailoring the depth of technical detail to the audience.
Exposure to AI/ML or enterprise data initiatives is preferred.
Experience in media, entertainment, or similarly fast-moving industries is preferred.

What You Will Get

The unique and exciting opportunity to work at one of a leading global entertainment companies
Access to the tools, leadership, and resources you will need to create and drive a center of excellence
The opportunity to do the best work of your career
Work in an inclusive and diverse company culture
Competitive programs to support your well-being
Experience working in a collaborative environment with room to grow

UTA is a premier global talent agency built for the future of media and entertainment. The agency's diversified platform and best-in-class, client-first approach is innovative, collaborative, and positioned to lead in an evolving market. UTA represents the most celebrated artists, creatives, and brands, from icons and legends to next-generation talent. Its integrated capabilities span film and television, music, comedy, creators, sports, brands, news, publishing, speakers, theater, and more. It is based in Los Angeles with offices in the U.S., London, and Munich.

new_jobs.title: Senior IT Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Sopra Steria
offers tailored, end-to-end corporate technology and software solutions to help clients make bold choices and deliver results. Successfully so! With more than 56.000 colleagues in 30 countries, we rank as Europe’s leading digital solutions provider. Some of the most successful companies in Europe rely on our technology due to our commitment to innovation, collaboration, and value in business development.

The world is how we shape it. Let’s shape it together.

Job Description

The Senior IT Programme Manager
will serve as the single accountable executive for a flagship European Commission programme in the domains of Dataspace and Artificial Intelligence. Operating at the intersection of cutting-edge technology policy and large-scale public-sector delivery, this individual will bear ultimate responsibility for scope, schedule, budget, quality, risk, and stakeholder satisfaction across a multi-partner consortium delivering transformative digital infrastructure for Europe.

This is a highly visible, strategically critical position requiring a rare combination of deep EU institutional knowledge, technical credibility in Dataspace and AI, and the executive presence to lead complex negotiations at the highest levels of the European Commission and across 27 Member State administrations.

Key Responsibilities:

Programme Leadership & Governance
Establish and chair the Programme Governance Board, ensuring alignment with European Commission priorities and contractual obligations.
Define and own the integrated programme master plan (IMP), managing interdependencies across all workstreams and consortium partners.
Drive end-to-end programme execution from inception through deployment and operational handover, maintaining a €100M+ budget baseline.
Apply and adapt EU programme management frameworks (e.g., PM²) and Agile-at-scale methodologies as appropriate.
Own programme-level risk register, issue log, and escalation procedures; proactively identify and mitigate threats to delivery.
Consortium Leadership & Partner Management
Lead the operational governance of a consortium comprising four partner organisations, including sub-contractor oversight and contractual compliance.
Chair and facilitate Consortium Management Committees, Technical Steering Committees, and Joint Programme Boards.
Manage partner performance, monitor KPIs, and enforce SLAs and contractual obligations under the prime contract.
Resolve cross-partner conflicts, resource contention, and scope boundary disputes with authority and diplomacy.
Foster a collaborative, high-performance consortium culture aligned with shared programme objectives.
EU Institutional Stakeholder Management
Serve as the primary relationship owner and executive point of contact for European Commission DG counterparts.
Build and sustain trusted advisory relationships with Commission programme sponsors, IT Steering Committees, and EC senior management.
Engage proactively with EU country stakeholders across 27 Member States, coordinating national rollout activities and managing country-level expectations.
Represent the programme in high-level review meetings, governance forums, and political-level briefings.
Navigate the EU institutional landscape with sensitivity to political dynamics, procurement regulations, and EU financial regulations.
Dataspace & AI Programme Delivery
Oversee technical delivery of Dataspace architecture components.
Drive AI programme workstreams in alignment with the EU AI Act, the AI Office, and Commission AI strategies.
Ensure technical solutions are interoperable, standards-compliant (EUCS, ETSI, W3C, ISO), and aligned with EU security requirements.
Collaborate with Enterprise Architects, Data Engineers, Developers, testers and AI specialists to validate technical direction and manage delivery risk.
Financial Management
Own and manage the full programme budget (€100M+), including baseline, forecast, earned value management (EVM), and variance reporting.
Oversee procurement activities under EU Financial Regulations and applicable framework contracts.
Prepare and defend financial reports, Monthly Progress Reports (MPR), and Quarterly Management Reviews for the Commission.
Ensure auditability of programme expenditure in accordance with EC Internal Audit Service (IAS) standards.
Quality, Compliance & Reporting
Implement and maintain the Quality Management Plan (QMP) in accordance with ISO 9001 and EC quality standards.
Ensure compliance with GDPR, NIS2, EU AI Act, and relevant Commission security policies (ITSM, ISMS).
Produce executive-level programme dashboards, milestone reports, and presentations for senior EC stakeholders.
Manage lessons learned, continuous improvement, and knowledge transfer processes throughout the programme lifecycle.

Qualifications

Minimum 15 years of IT programme/project management experience, with at least 8 years in senior/lead programme management/director roles.
Demonstrated track record of successfully delivering EU Commission IT programmes at scale (€50M+ budget), ideally with DGs like DIGIT, TAXUD, CONNECT, or equivalent.
Proven experience managing and leading multi-partner consortia as prime contractor in EU public procurement contexts.
Deep operational knowledge of EU procurement frameworks, framework contracts, and EU Financial Regulations.
Hands-on experience with EU programme management methodology PM² or equivalent, including governance, reporting, and documentation standards.
Experience engaging with EU Member State government stakeholders and national administrations across multiple countries.
Substantial technical exposure to Dataspace architectures and/or AI programme delivery in a public sector or regulated environment.

Highly Desirable

Direct experience on EU Dataspace programmes (e.g., GAIA-X, IDSA-aligned, European Health Data Space, Mobility Data Space, or similar).
Knowledge of EU AI initiatives including the EU AI Act implementation, the European AI Office, and AI regulatory compliance frameworks.
Familiarity with EC digital infrastructure programmes such as CEF Digital, the Digital Europe Programme (DEP), or Horizon Europe ICT projects.
Experience with EC interoperability frameworks (EIF) and the ISA²/Interoperable Europe Act.
Understanding of cloud sovereign requirements under EUCS and European cloud initiatives.

Education & Certifications

Master's degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Public Administration, or a related field.
Programme/Project Management: PgMP (PMI), MSP (AXELOS), or PM² Advanced certification required.
Desirable: PMP, PRINCE2 Practitioner, ITIL 4 Foundation, Scrum@Scale, or SAFe certification.
EU institutional training or EPSO-related qualifications are an advantage.

Additional Information

Why Sopra Steria?

Work at the intersection of business strategy and technology transformation.
Contribute to large-scale, high-impact digital programmes.
Be part of a leading European consulting and digital services organisation.

What we offer?

A strategically pivotal role shaping Europe's digital infrastructure for a decade to come.
Direct engagement at the highest levels of the European Commission and EU Member State governments.

Drive the future of AI Transformation at Pearson as part of the AI Centre for Enablement team (AI C4E). Inspire innovation. Empower learning.

Pearson, the world's leading learning company, is hiring a Program Manager, AI Control Plane
for our Office of Chief Technology Officer (OCTO)
to join the AI Centre for Enablement (C4E) team.

Why This Role Matters:

The AI Control Plane (AICP) is Pearson's flagship investment in AI infrastructure: a multi-year programme that closes Pearson's AI governance gap, accelerates how teams ship AI value, and builds the strategic know-how to keep AI cost-effective as usage scales. It delivers enterprise-wide visibility into Pearson's AI estate—what is deployed, what it costs, where it creates value, and what we should do next. AICP sits inside OCTO's AI Centre for Enablement (C4E).
This is a deliberately blended role. Roughly 70% is technical programme management of a major cross-organisation investment, working across Pearson business units and corporate functions including engineering, security, and legal. Roughly 30% is product leadership for an internal 'data product'—the enterprise AI telemetry dashboard that turns Pearson's AI investment decisions from opinion-led to evidence-led. You will drive how that dashboard looks and how it gets built, working with a cross-functional engineering pod inside OCTO.
You run the day-to-day delivery of AICP—from architecture handoff through business-unit onboarding to global scale—and act as product owner for the enterprise AI telemetry dashboard. You free the engineering and architecture leads from coordination overhead so they can focus on what only they can do.
As a member of OCTO AI C4E and Pearson, you are expected to embody and role model our leadership dimensions:

Live Our Purpose:
You align your values, actions, and goals with Pearson's mission. You connect daily work to our broader purpose and make decisions that reflect a deep understanding of our strategy.

Simplify the Complexity:
You navigate ambiguity and distil complexity into clear, actionable plans. You help teams focus and execute in a dynamic environment.

Carry Our Culture:
You foster customer centricity, high performance, and strong collaboration. You lead with integrity and contribute to inclusive, high-performing teams.

Deliver Results:
You set ambitious goals and execute with quality, precision, and speed. You hold yourself accountable for outcomes and measurable impact for learners and stakeholders.

What You'll Do

Translate AICP strategy into executable plans—workstreams, owners, milestones, dependencies—across Pearson business units and corporate functions including engineering, security, and legal.
Run programme cadence and reporting: status, risks, decision logs, steering committees, working groups. Coordinate external delivery partners against contractual commitments and commercial terms.
Drive business-unit adoption of the governance and security capabilities AICP delivers—discovery, risk tiering, monitoring—against ambitious year-end onboarding targets.
Act as product owner for the enterprise AI telemetry dashboard: define personas and the questions they need answered, prioritise the backlog, and ship v1 covering an initial set of enterprise tools. Build prototypes and design mocks where it helps the engineering team move faster.

Who You Are:

Customer-centric: you keep business-unit outcomes and leadership decisions—not vendor outputs—as the success measure.
Hands-on and AI-fluent: you mock up a dashboard, prototype with modern AI tools, and drive design decisions yourself rather than waiting for engineers to read your mind.
Pragmatic and persistent: you create clarity where none exists and close follow-up loops before they become escalations.

What You Bring

5+ years of programme or project management in technology, with cross-functional reach across product, engineering, and operations.
Product management or product-owner experience for technical or data products—someone who has shipped a v1 of something internal, not just managed a backlog.
Vendor coordination experience with major enterprise technology partners (e.g. hyperscalers, large system integrators).
Working understanding of AI, data engineering, or cloud architecture at a level sufficient to translate technical constraints into delivery plans and product decisions.

What You'll Gain:

Lead-PM/PdM role on a Board-visible AI infrastructure programme sponsored by OCTO leadership.
Ownership of the enterprise AI telemetry product—Pearson's first enterprise view of "what AI is doing for us".
Direct collaboration with engineering, security, and business-unit leaders across Pearson, and visibility across OCTO and the Chief Data & AI Office.

Why Pearson?

At Pearson, we don't just build careers—we accelerate them. This position provides visibility across the Office of the Chief Technology Officer and the AI C4E, with a clear path into broader technical and strategic roles.
We believe great work deserves great rewards. We offer competitive benefits designed to support the diverse needs of our people and their families. Explore our Benefits.

Apply today and imagine the impact you can make.

Bolt is shaping a future where cities are built for people, not cars. What started as an ambitious project of a 19-year-old in 2013 has grown into a global mobility platform used by more than 200 million customers and 4.5 million driver and courier partners across 50 countries.

From ride-hailing and food delivery to scooters, e-bikes, and car-sharing, Bolt helps people move through cities every day. Small, autonomous teams drive this work, combining the speed and ownership of a startup with the scale of a global technology company backed by more than €1bn in funding.

And we're just getting started.

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗷𝗼𝗶𝗻 𝗕𝗼𝗹𝘁?

Build the future of mobility and help transform how people live and move in cities.
Tackle challenges at scale that span technology, operations, regulation, and growth.
Take real ownership early. Small, lean teams mean your decisions matter from day one, and you'll learn fast alongside some of the best people in the industry.
Join one of Europe's leading technology companies, backed by world-class investors including Sequoia.

𝗔𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗼𝗹𝗲

Our Central Safety Team monitors and prevents risks that could cause real-world harm to users.

As Program Manager, Safety Processes & Enforcement, you'll own the translation layer between safety policy and operational execution: converting policy intent into enforcement standards, account restriction decisions and case-handling processes that Customer Support agents can apply consistently across every case and every market, supported by automation where appropriate.

You'll own the suspension matrix that determines the enforcement logic for each type of violation, the SOP library that tells support agents how to get there, and the specification work that makes those processes ready for automation, with human oversight built in.

𝗠𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗮𝘀𝗸𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗲𝘀:

Own the suspension matrix and severity classification: define and maintain the enforcement ladder that maps each violation type and severity level to an account action for both riders and partner drivers, with one shared definition of severity used for enforcement decisions and incident response.
Build and maintain the SOP library for all safety issue areas, making sure every policy position has a process agents can follow and no process contradicts the enforcement standards. Write processes ready for automation (clear decision trees, defined inputs and outputs, explicit exception and fallback paths) and work with Product and Legal to specify rules-engine logic and automation-assisted enforcement flows, with human review built in.
Own the quality rubric and calibration standards for safety case handling, and own appeals standards by defining how appeals are assessed and what can overturn an enforcement decision.
Drive enforcement consistency: run regular audits, measure where outcomes differ across agents and markets, and lead the fixes.
Work with Safety Policy to make sure standards reflect policy intent, and with Local Safety Operations on local process deviations, making sure each one is documented, justified and checked against the global standard. Report on enforcement consistency, process coverage and automation readiness against team KPIs.

𝗔𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝘆𝗼𝘂:

Proven experience in Trust & Safety, risk management, policy operations or a comparable field, including direct ownership of enforcement policy or operational process design at scale.
Demonstrated experience building or overhauling an SOP library, enforcement framework or suspension matrix used by a large operational team, and writing process specifications for automation or working alongside Product and Engineering on rules engines.
Working knowledge of regulation affecting account enforcement and automated decision-making, such as GDPR, the EU Platform Work Directive and the Digital Services Act.
Deep knowledge of enforcement policy design and policy-to-process translation, with end-to-end ownership of the enforcement framework: you anticipate where standards will drift or break under volume and fix it before it becomes an incident, using case data, appeals data and quality metrics to see where standards are failing in practice.
Strong collaboration and influencing skills across product, legal and operations teams, building agreement without formal authority and holding the line on enforcement consistency under commercial or operational pressure, while managing interdependent workstreams in the right order (standards before processes, processes before automation) and adapting to evolving priorities.

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝘆𝗼𝘂'𝗹𝗹 𝗹𝗼𝘃𝗲 𝗶𝘁 𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲
